# Daily auto-publish (issue #161): thin orchestrator over the existing
# publish channels. Each channel is an isolated leg — one leg failing never
# kills the others — and every failure self-files a deduplicated GitHub
# issue (label `bug`, assigned to the owner) that auto-closes when the leg
# goes green again. No publish logic is duplicated here: legs dispatch the
# existing workflows via `gh workflow run` and watch them.
#
#   testflight  build-mobile.yml   ios_content=all (the iOS half of the
#                                 mobile build)
#   play        build-mobile.yml   android_content=all,
#                                 android_track=beta (Android external
#                                 beta / open testing — issue #289 lifts
#                                 the standing "Android excluded" owner
#                                 decision for the release track; #947
#                                 adds the listing deploy — texts +
#                                 whole-set image replace + verify — so
#                                 the listing never trails the goldens;
#                                 the leg green-skips while the Play
#                                 secrets are absent)
#   pubdev      in-job OIDC publish, only when pubspec > pub.dev; otherwise
#               a green up-to-date check. The tag-time OIDC publish job
#               (ci.yml) stays the primary path; this leg is the catch-up +
#               loud-failure detector (e.g. expired publish credentials)
#   cli         build-macos.yml    desktop DMG + macOS CLI bundles +
#                                 extension, attached to the next-tag
#                                 release (version passed explicitly so
#                                 mobile/desktop never mint diverging tags)
#   website     pages.yml          fa1.dev (landing + web demo +
#                                 the /outlook add-in slice; gh-1684:
#                                 the extension zip moved to GitHub
#                                 Releases and is no longer site-hosted)
#   addin       office-addin.yml   manifest/taskpane acceptance suite; the
#                                 fa1.dev publish itself rides the website
#                                 leg (pages.yml assembles /outlook)
#
# Legs run only when main moved since the last GREEN daily run — skip-no-
# change is green-neutral, never red (#159 lesson). One exception (gh-1192):
# while main's pubspec version is not yet served by pub.dev the plan gate
# (scripts/daily_plan.sh) forces the legs anyway — a release-in-flight
# green must not become a skip baseline that stalls re-verification and
# rerun-recovery on a quiet main. Versioning stays the
# existing scheme: auto_release.sh patch-bumps + tags every main push
# (2h coalesce); the daily attaches mobile/desktop artifacts to the next
# tag and verifies/republishes pub.dev. See docs/ci.md.
#
# Pause: gh workflow disable daily-publish.yml -R IstiN/flutter_agent_harness

name: Daily auto-publish

run-name: "Daily auto-publish (${{ inputs.legs || 'all' }})"

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '17 5 * * *' # once daily, 05:17 UTC
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      legs:
        description: 'Leg(s) to run'
        type: choice
        default: all
        options:
          - all
          - testflight
          - play
          - pubdev
          - cli
          - website
          - addin
      force:
        description: 'Run even if main has not moved since the last green daily'
        type: boolean
        default: false
      inject_failure:
        description: 'TEST ONLY — fail this leg before any dispatch, to exercise the self-filing issue cycle'
        type: choice
        default: none
        options:
          - none
          - testflight
          - play
          - pubdev
          - cli
          - website
          - addin

permissions:
  contents: read

# One daily at a time; a queued run must not cancel an in-flight one.
concurrency:
  group: daily-publish
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  plan:
    name: Plan (change detection + versions)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # gh-1477: 10m was the same time bomb as the derive-version jobs — a
    # full-history fetch under a 10m ceiling. 20m + the blobless filter
    # below.
    timeout-minutes: 20
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: read
    outputs:
      changed: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.changed }}
      next_tag: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.next_tag }}
      latest_tag: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.latest_tag }}
      pubspec_version: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.pubspec_version }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          # gh-1477: daily_plan.sh reads tags / commit metadata / one file
          # at origin/main — never historical blobs. Blobless keeps full
          # tag/commit metadata without the blobs (the full fetch outgrew
          # the old 10m ceiling in the twin derive-version job, run
          # 38027695551).
          fetch-depth: 0
          filter: blob:none

      - name: Detect main movement and derive versions
        id: plan
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          FORCE: ${{ inputs.force }}
        # gh-1192: the gate (baseline + the release-unresolved re-arm that
        # keeps AC1's «the next daily re-verifies» true on a quiet main)
        # lives in the extracted script — shell-harness tested by
        # test/release_flow_race_test.dart.
        run: bash scripts/daily_plan.sh

  # ── Dispatch legs ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Shape per leg: dispatch the child workflow pinned to main, capture the
  # new run id, wait for it read-only, fail on any non-success conclusion.
  # The child run URL is exported even on failure so the report can excerpt
  # its log.
  #
  # ── The gh-1903 invariant: queued on the single self-hosted runner is
  # HEALTHY ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # dispatch_and_watch.sh NEVER cancels or re-dispatches a child mid-watch.
  # A child queued behind siblings on the shared fa-m5-1 is normal
  # operation; the old #344 budget + gh-172 queue-stall watchdog cancelled
  # two such healthy queued children on 2026-10-26 (daily run 40274465122,
  # tracking issue #1735 — those cancellations were THIS defect, not an
  # ASC/IPA problem) and failed a fully-built v1.0.648 solely by killing
  # its place in line. What bounds a slow child instead:
  #   * every job in a watched child chain carries an explicit
  #     timeout-minutes — a wedged self-hosted job self-fails server-side
  #     (#344; a job-level timeout is enforced BY the runner, which is why
  #     a hung worker outliving its own ceiling is the one class the
  #     server cannot kill), and
  #   * the leg timeout-minutes below — when it fires, the runner TERMs
  #     the watcher, which cancels ONLY this leg's own NEVER-STARTED child
  #     (gh-1903 orphan-cancel) so an orphaned queued run cannot publish
  #     unattended, then fails naming the child run, its last observed
  #     state, and the observed pool activity (gh-172 diagnostic).
  # While the child has not started, the watcher logs sibling in-progress
  # runs on a diagnostic interval — read-only; cannot-observe ⇒
  # cannot-judge ⇒ never a cancel.
  #
  # ── Timeout arithmetic (#351, leg-timeout sizing) ────────────────────────
  # Child worst-case = sum of the serialized job timeout-minutes along the
  # child's critical path (every job in a watched chain carries an explicit
  # timeout for exactly this). Invariant: leg timeout > child worst-case +
  # margin (appear window 60×10s ≈ 10m + poll slack ≈ 5m) — the leg always
  # outlives a healthy slow child, which is now NEVER killed.
  #
  #   leg        child worst-case (serialized chain)          leg timeout
  #   testflight version 20 → build-ios 90 → submit-ios 120   230m  ;  360m
  #             (∥ release-mobile 15, covered by the max)
  #   play       version 20 → build-android 45 →              95m   ;  240m
  #             submit-android 30 (∥ release-mobile 15)
  #   cli        version 20 → build-macos 150×2 (arm64 +      335m  ;  360m
  #             x86_64 SERIALIZE on the single self-hosted
  #             runner) → release-macos 15
  #             (∥ cli matrix 45, extension 30 — shorter paths)
  #   (gh-1477: the version/plan jobs' ceiling moved 10 → 20m — a
  #   full-history fetch outgrew the 10m bomb; the fetch is now blobless
  #   and 20m is the seatbelt. Worst-cases grew by exactly the +10m.)
  #   website    pages build 45 → deploy 15                   60m   ;  180m
  #   addin      office-addin-suite 45 (single job)           45m   ;  150m
  #
  # gh-172 (run 39374894901, 2026-10-20) history: the re-dispatched
  # testflight child sat queued FOREVER on the zombie self-hosted worker —
  # the leg burned its remaining ~107m and died as a bare 360m ceiling
  # kill with no diagnosis. The budget/stall watchdog built to catch that
  # faster could not tell a zombie-held pool from a sibling leg's job
  # legitimately occupying the shared fa-m5-1 (its own comment admitted
  # it), and its 31m stall window did not cover the cli sibling chain's
  # 335m worst-case — so it false-cancelled healthy queues by design
  # (gh-1903, #1735). The zombie goal is now met by the bounds above plus
  # the leg-timeout orphan-cancel diagnostic, not by a heuristic that
  # cannot tell a queue from a zombie.

  testflight:
    name: 'Leg: TestFlight'
    needs: plan
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # #351 arithmetic: child wc 230m (version 20 + build-ios 90 +
    # submit-ios 120); 360m leg > worst-case + ~15m margin. The 360m cap
    # also bounds any gh-172 zombie wait — on leg timeout the watcher's
    # orphan-cancel kills only this leg's never-started child (gh-1903).
    timeout-minutes: 360
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: write
    if: >-
      (needs.plan.outputs.changed == 'true' || inputs.force == true) &&
      (inputs.legs == '' || inputs.legs == 'all' || inputs.legs == 'testflight')
    outputs:
      run_url: ${{ steps.dispatch.outputs.run_url }}
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Inject failure (test)
        if: inputs.inject_failure == 'testflight'
        run: |
          echo "::error::injected failure (inject_failure=testflight) — exercising the self-filing issue path, nothing dispatched"
          exit 1

      - name: Dispatch build-mobile.yml and watch
        id: dispatch
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # Shared watcher (gh-1903, correlation from #343): correlates
          # OUR run by the child's run-name ("build-mobile (none/all)" —
          # displayTitle is the only distinguisher in the run-list API),
          # newest match in a tight window. Waits READ-ONLY: a child
          # queued behind siblings on the shared fa-m5-1 is healthy and is
          # never cancelled/re-dispatched; the bounds are build-ios/
          # submit-ios's own timeout-minutes (#344) and this leg's 360m.
          # On leg timeout the watcher cancels only this leg's own
          # never-started orphan child (gh-1903) — see the leg-header
          # comment for the full invariant.
          rc=0
          bash scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh build-mobile.yml \
            --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" --ref main \
            --title 'build-mobile (none/all)' \
            -f android_content=none -f ios_content=all \
            --out-run-id run_id.txt || rc=$?
          if [ -s run_id.txt ]; then
            echo "run_url=https://github.com/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/actions/runs/$(cat run_id.txt)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi
          exit "$rc"

  play:
    name: 'Leg: Play (Android external beta)'
    # Independent of the testflight leg (#359). The #348 serialization was
    # a mitigation for the #343 sibling-dispatch race; #351 eliminated that
    # race structurally — exact displayTitle correlation (this leg's child
    # runs as "build-mobile (all/none)", the testflight leg's as
    # "(none/all)"), NEWEST match, a tight 30s window, and build-mobile's
    # per-run_id concurrency group (no dispatch can cancel another). With
    # the race gone the needs-edge only bought harm: a cancelled testflight
    # watcher skipped Play behind it and the edge added up to 360m of start
    # latency (one leg's external blocker stopped the train — run
    # 34827074052, BETA_REVIEW_CONTACT_EMAIL user-owned).
    #
    # The two residual #346 concerns are handled structurally, not by
    # ordering:
    #   * same-tag convergence — both children independently derive
    #     latest-tag+1, so they can attach to ONE release concurrently;
    #     release_attach_or_create.sh is race-idempotent (a lost create
    #     uploads into the winner's release) with an ownership-scoped draft
    #     guard, and the asset sets never collide (AAB vs IPA).
    #   * runner contention — none: the Android chain is all GitHub-hosted
    #     runners; only build-ios touches the single self-hosted macOS
    #     runner (which already serializes physically with the cli leg's
    #     build-macos children — that pair has always been independent).
    needs: plan
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # #351 arithmetic (unchanged by #359 — only the leg's START moved):
    # child wc 95m (version 20 + build-android 45 + submit-android 30);
    # 240m leg > worst-case + ~15m margin. Waits are read-only (gh-1903) —
    # no cancel, no re-dispatch, bounded by the child's per-job timeouts
    # (#344) and this leg timeout.
    timeout-minutes: 240
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: write
    if: >-
      (needs.plan.outputs.changed == 'true' || inputs.force == true) &&
      (inputs.legs == '' || inputs.legs == 'all' || inputs.legs == 'play')
    outputs:
      run_url: ${{ steps.dispatch.outputs.run_url }}
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
      # Secrets presence is checked in the first step — while the Play
      # upload keystore/service account are not configured, the leg green-
      # skips with a notice (existing neutral-skip leg semantics); it goes
      # live the moment the owner sets them (issue #289).
      PLAY_STORE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON: ${{ secrets.PLAY_STORE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON }}
      ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64 }}
      ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD }}
      ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS }}
      ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Inject failure (test)
        if: inputs.inject_failure == 'play'
        run: |
          echo "::error::injected failure (inject_failure=play) — exercising the self-filing issue path, nothing dispatched"
          exit 1

      - name: Skip without Play secrets (green-neutral)
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          missing=""
          [ -z "${ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64:-}" ] && missing="$missing ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64"
          [ -z "${ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD:-}" ] && missing="$missing ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD"
          [ -z "${ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS:-}" ] && missing="$missing ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS"
          [ -z "${ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD:-}" ] && missing="$missing ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD"
          if [ -z "${PLAY_STORE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON:-}" ]; then
            missing="$missing PLAY_STORE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON"
          fi
          if [ -n "$missing" ]; then
            echo "::notice::Play secrets not configured (missing:${missing}) — the Android leg skips green-neutrally until the upload keystore + Play service account secrets exist (issue #289 owner checklist)."
            exit 0
          fi
          echo "All Play secrets present — dispatching the Android build+upload."

      - name: Dispatch build-mobile.yml and watch
        id: dispatch
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # all: build + Play upload + LISTING deploy (issue #947) — the
          # listing lane replaces the whole image set per locale + device
          # type and verifies it via edits.images.list, so the listing can
          # never trail the committed goldens by more than one train.
          # beta = the external/open testing track, mirroring the iOS leg's
          # external TestFlight group (#239 pattern).
          # Shared watcher (gh-1903 read-only wait; correlation from #343).
          # Since #359 the TestFlight
          # sibling leg fires CONCURRENTLY with this one (both needs: plan)
          # and dispatches the SAME workflow in the same minute —
          # correlation is by the child's run-name ("build-mobile
          # (all/none)" vs the sibling's "(none/all)", pinned by
          # test), never by "first run in the window", with newest-match +
          # the 30s window. Read-only wait (gh-1903): a wedged/queued run
          # is NEVER cancelled or re-dispatched — build-android/submit-
          # android's own timeout-minutes (#344) and this leg's 240m are
          # the only bounds; on leg timeout only this leg's own
          # never-started orphan child is cancelled.
          rc=0
          bash scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh build-mobile.yml \
            --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" --ref main \
            --title 'build-mobile (all/none)' \
            -f android_content=all -f android_track=beta -f ios_content=none \
            --out-run-id run_id.txt || rc=$?
          if [ -s run_id.txt ]; then
            echo "run_url=https://github.com/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/actions/runs/$(cat run_id.txt)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi
          exit "$rc"

  cli:
    name: 'Leg: CLI + macOS desktop'
    needs: plan
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # #351 arithmetic: child wc 335m (version 20 + build-macos 150×2 — the
    # arm64 AND x86_64 matrix legs SERIALIZE on the single self-hosted
    # macOS runner — + release-macos 15); 360m leg ≥ worst-case + margin
    # (both build-macos jobs carry 150m server-side timeouts, #344). A
    # queued child — including one waiting out a sibling's full 150m
    # matrix leg — is NEVER cancelled (gh-1903); the leg timeout bounds
    # the wait and the watcher orphan-cancels only a never-started child.
    timeout-minutes: 360
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: write
    if: >-
      (needs.plan.outputs.changed == 'true' || inputs.force == true) &&
      (inputs.legs == '' || inputs.legs == 'all' || inputs.legs == 'cli')
    outputs:
      run_url: ${{ steps.dispatch.outputs.run_url }}
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Inject failure (test)
        if: inputs.inject_failure == 'cli'
        run: |
          echo "::error::injected failure (inject_failure=cli) — exercising the self-filing issue path, nothing dispatched"
          exit 1

      - name: Dispatch build-macos.yml and watch
        id: dispatch
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # Children derive version themselves (latest tag + 1 at their own
          # dispatch moment) — a tag pinned here would race auto_release and
          # could attach assets to a tag pointing at a different commit.
          # Shared watcher (gh-1903 read-only wait; correlation from #343):
          # correlates OUR run by the child's run-name
          # ("build-macos (create_release=true)") so a concurrent human
          # dispatch is never adopted. A wedged self-hosted run is NEVER
          # cancelled/re-dispatched — the bounds are the build-macos jobs'
          # own 150m server-side timeouts (#344) and this leg's 360m; on
          # leg timeout the watcher orphan-cancels only this leg's own
          # never-started child.
          rc=0
          bash scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh build-macos.yml \
            --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" --ref main \
            --title 'build-macos (create_release=true)' \
            -f create_release=true \
            --out-run-id run_id.txt || rc=$?
          if [ -s run_id.txt ]; then
            echo "run_url=https://github.com/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/actions/runs/$(cat run_id.txt)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi
          exit "$rc"

  website:
    name: 'Leg: Website'
    needs: plan
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # #351 arithmetic: child wc 60m (pages build 45 + deploy 15); 180m leg
    # ≫ worst-case + margin. (The old 45m leg pre-dated #351 and could not
    # even fit a healthy child + appear window — the 180m leg is the
    # #351 sizing.)
    timeout-minutes: 180
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: write
    if: >-
      (needs.plan.outputs.changed == 'true' || inputs.force == true) &&
      (inputs.legs == '' || inputs.legs == 'all' || inputs.legs == 'website')
    outputs:
      run_url: ${{ steps.dispatch.outputs.run_url }}
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Inject failure (test)
        if: inputs.inject_failure == 'website'
        run: |
          echo "::error::injected failure (inject_failure=website) — exercising the self-filing issue path, nothing dispatched"
          exit 1

      # pages.yml is path-filtered on push, so routine pushes (e.g. lib/
      # changes outside its filters) never redeploy — the daily guarantees
      # fa1.dev tracks main.
      - name: Dispatch pages.yml and watch
        id: dispatch
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # Shared watcher (gh-1903 read-only wait; correlation from #343).
          # pages.yml takes no inputs, so there is no displayTitle to
          # disambiguate on — the watcher falls back to
          # newest-in-tight-window and waits read-only: no cancel, no
          # re-dispatch, bounded by the pages jobs' own timeout-minutes
          # (#344) and this leg's 180m.
          rc=0
          bash scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh pages.yml \
            --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" --ref main \
            --out-run-id run_id.txt || rc=$?
          if [ -s run_id.txt ]; then
            echo "run_url=https://github.com/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/actions/runs/$(cat run_id.txt)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi
          exit "$rc"

  addin:
    name: 'Leg: Outlook add-in'
    needs: plan
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # #351 arithmetic: child wc 45m (single office-addin-suite job); 150m
    # leg ≫ worst-case + margin. (The old 45m leg pre-dated #351 and could
    # not even fit a healthy child + appear window — 150m is the #351
    # sizing.)
    timeout-minutes: 150
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: write
    if: >-
      (needs.plan.outputs.changed == 'true' || inputs.force == true) &&
      (inputs.legs == '' || inputs.legs == 'all' || inputs.legs == 'addin')
    outputs:
      run_url: ${{ steps.dispatch.outputs.run_url }}
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Inject failure (test)
        if: inputs.inject_failure == 'addin'
        run: |
          echo "::error::injected failure (inject_failure=addin) — exercising the self-filing issue path, nothing dispatched"
          exit 1

      # Acceptance suite (manifest validation, dart2js taskpane, Node +
      # Playwright e2e). The fa1.dev /outlook publish itself rides the
      # website leg — pages.yml assembles the same add-in into the deploy.
      - name: Dispatch office-addin.yml and watch
        id: dispatch
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # Shared watcher (gh-1903 read-only wait; correlation from #343).
          # No inputs to disambiguate on (newest-in-tight-window
          # fallback); the wait is bounded by the office-addin-suite
          # job's own 45m timeout (#344) and this leg's 150m — never by a
          # watcher cancel.
          rc=0
          bash scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh office-addin.yml \
            --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" --ref main \
            --out-run-id run_id.txt || rc=$?
          if [ -s run_id.txt ]; then
            echo "run_url=https://github.com/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/actions/runs/$(cat run_id.txt)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi
          exit "$rc"

  # ── pub.dev leg ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # The ONLY publish path is the ci.yml tag job (pub.dev trusted publishing
  # only accepts OIDC from tag-push runs — a schedule/dispatch run can never
  # satisfy it). This leg VERIFIES pub.dev serves the pubspec version and,
  # when behind, recovers by re-running the failed tag-push publish run —
  # a rerun keeps the original push-tag event and OIDC claims, so the real
  # publish path retries. Unrecoverable states fail loudly and self-file an
  # issue with a manual-publish instruction instead of silently hanging.
  # gh-1192: a tag-publish still EXECUTING (tag pushed, ci run not visible
  # yet or queued/in_progress, tag younger than the grace window) is
  # classified «release in flight» by scripts/verify_pubdev_release.sh —
  # a neutral skip (no error, no auto-filed issue); the next scheduled
  # daily re-verifies. The 2026-10-03 collision fired the old «no ci.yml
  # run» error one minute before the healthy run completed (#1189, false
  # alarm). gh-1522: the version under test is the LATEST REMOTE TAG (the
  # committed pubspec is the 0.0.0-dev placeholder), so the «tag not cut
  # yet» state no longer exists.

    name: 'Leg: pub.dev'
    needs: plan
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 60
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: write # gh run rerun of the tag-publish run

      (needs.plan.outputs.changed == 'true' || inputs.force == true) &&
      (inputs.legs == '' || inputs.legs == 'all' || inputs.legs == 'pubdev')

      status: ${{ steps.check.outputs.status }}

      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}

      - name: Inject failure (test)

      # the fa-release-bot App token — a GITHUB_TOKEN push can never cascade
      # (gh-1172), the App's push can (the same mechanism ci.yml's release
      # job uses to cut tags). Job-scoped, expires with the job; this job's
      # own GITHUB_TOKEN stays read-scoped (job-level permissions block).
      # Shape mirrors the validator-proven precedent (ci.yml release job,
      # the create-github-app-token step): NO `if:` at all — secrets
      # context in a step-if trips GitHub's workflow validator; and a mint

      # continue-on-error, outputs.token stays empty, and the script's
      # manual-re-push alarm fires exactly as before this change.

      # does NOT exist there (action.yml defines only the generated
      # `permission-*` inputs — GitHub warns `Unexpected input(s)
      # 'permissions'` and the action never reads it; ci.yml:3980 rides
      # that warning). The HONORED ceiling is the granular
      # `permission-contents` input, which the action turns into the mint
      # request's permissions map: contents:write only — the tag re-push —
      # instead of the installation's full grant set. Without it the token
      # inherits every permission the fa-release-bot installation has.

    if: always() # even when plan failed or all legs skipped
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    permissions:
      contents: write # delete draft releases
      actions: read # name each swept draft's creating run (gh run list 403s without it, review of #294)
      issues: write # deduplicated self-closing sweep issue
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Delete drafts older than 24h and file the dedup issue

    name: Summary + self-filed issues
    needs: [plan, testflight, play, pubdev, cli, website, addin]

    permissions:

      actions: read
      issues: write
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Job summary table and issue lifecycle
        env:
          NEXT_TAG: ${{ needs.plan.outputs.next_tag }}
          PLAN_RESULT: ${{ needs.plan.result }}
          DAILY_PUBLISH_ASSIGNEE: ai-teammate
          LEG_TESTFLIGHT: ${{ needs.testflight.result }}
          LEG_TESTFLIGHT_URL: ${{ needs.testflight.outputs.run_url }}
          LEG_PLAY: ${{ needs.play.result }}
          LEG_PLAY_URL: ${{ needs.play.outputs.run_url }}
          LEG_PUBDEV: ${{ needs.pubdev.result }}
          LEG_PUBDEV_STATUS: ${{ needs.pubdev.outputs.status }}
          LEG_PUBDEV_PUBSPEC: ${{ needs.pubdev.outputs.pubspec_version }}
          LEG_PUBDEV_PUBLISHED: ${{ needs.pubdev.outputs.published_version }}
          LEG_PUBDEV_URL: ${{ needs.pubdev.outputs.run_url }}
          LEG_CLI: ${{ needs.cli.result }}
          LEG_CLI_URL: ${{ needs.cli.outputs.run_url }}
          LEG_WEBSITE: ${{ needs.website.result }}
          LEG_WEBSITE_URL: ${{ needs.website.outputs.run_url }}
          LEG_ADDIN: ${{ needs.addin.result }}

      # only on `!= 'none'` would run — and fail — this step every cron run.
      - name: Verify injected-failure excerpt (TEST)
        if: always() && inputs.inject_failure != '' && inputs.inject_failure != 'none'
        env:
          INJECTED: ${{ inputs.inject_failure }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          title="[daily-publish] ${INJECTED} leg failed"
          n=$(gh issue list --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" --state open \
                --label daily-publish --limit 200 \
                --json number,title --jq '.[] | [.number, .title] | @tsv' \

                  done | head -1)
          if [ -z "$n" ]; then

          fi
          text=$(gh issue view "$n" --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" \
                   --json body,comments --jq '.body, (.comments[]?.body // empty)')

            echo "::error::inject_failure verify: issue #${n} never quotes the injected ::error:: line — the signal-first excerpt regressed (gh-1478)"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "inject_failure verify OK: issue #${n} quotes the injected error line (gh-1478)"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Mint a release tag as an ANNOTATED tag pushed with a CI-firing token, and
# verify the tag train actually started (gh-2026). Shared by the two
# draft-capable create paths:
#
#   - scripts/release_attach_or_create.sh (build-macos.yml release-macos,
#     build-mobile.yml release-mobile) — the tag was DEFINITELY missing at
#     attach time;
#   - scripts/release_lazy_draft.sh (build-macos.yml build-macos-cli /
#     build-extension) — a `gh release create` for a missing ref would
#     REST-mint a lightweight API tag with NO push event (the v0.1.408
#     silent class, issue #597): no tag train, a stranded draft.
#
# Why this exists — the v1.0.663 / v1.0.665 stale drafts (gh-2026): the
# release legs pushed the annotated tag through the GH_TOKEN URL, but
# actions/checkout had already persisted the JOB token in the repo-local
# git config as `http.<host>/.extraheader = AUTHORIZATION: basic …`. That
# header outranks the URL-embedded credentials on the wire, so GitHub saw
# a GITHUB_TOKEN push — and GitHub NEVER fires workflow runs for
# GITHUB_TOKEN pushes (gh-1172; docs/ci.md "its token triggers the
# tag-scoped jobs, which GITHUB_TOKEN pushes never do"). Both legs stayed
# green, no tag run ever existed on the refs, the provenance-owned publish
# (gh-1801) never ran, and the daily sweeper deleted the drafts a day
# later. Two guards close the class:
#
#   1. strip the persisted extraheader(s) before the push — the same
#      cleanup the Actions runner's post-job step performs ("Removing HTTP
#      extra header") — so the URL's PAT credentials are what GitHub sees
#      and the push fires ci.yml's `push: tags: ['v*']` train;
#   2. verify the outcome: poll for any workflow run on the tag ref within
#      a bounded budget. A push that triggers nothing fails this script
#      LOUD (no draft is created — the caller never reaches its create
#      step), so the leg goes red with a self-explaining error instead of
#      stranding a draft for the sweeper.
#
# Usage: release_tag_mint.sh <tag>
# Env: GITHUB_REPOSITORY, GITHUB_RUN_ID, GITHUB_JOB, GITHUB_SHA (Actions
#      defaults), GH_TOKEN — a PAT/App token, NEVER the workflow
#      GITHUB_TOKEN (a GITHUB_TOKEN push succeeds but can never trigger
#      the train; static lint pins every call site's export).
#      RELEASE_TARGET_SHA overrides the tag target (defaults GITHUB_SHA).
#      RELEASE_TRAIN_VERIFY_TRIES (default 12) ×
#      RELEASE_TRAIN_VERIFY_SLEEP seconds (default 10) bound the
#      verification; the test harness shrinks both.
set -euo pipefail

tag="${1:?usage: release_tag_mint.sh <tag>}"
repo="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY:?GITHUB_REPOSITORY must be set}"

# Fail fast BEFORE the cryptic crash: the push URL below collapses to ''
# when GH_TOKEN is unset, and git's `fatal: bad repository ''` does not
# point at the env gap (run 39766453580, v1.0.626 mobile leg).
if [ -z "${GH_TOKEN:-}" ]; then
  echo "::error::tag $tag is missing but GH_TOKEN is not set — the annotated-tag push would run 'git push \"\"'. Set GH_TOKEN (PAT/App token) on the calling step, or the tag can never be minted here." >&2
  exit 1
fi

# Guard 1 — strip the persisted checkout credentials. actions/checkout
# (persist-credentials defaults true) leaves the job token as an
# `http.<host>/.extraheader` in the LOCAL git config; git sends that
# Authorization header on every request to the host, and it outranks the
# URL-embedded GH_TOKEN credentials — the minted push would authenticate
# as GITHUB_TOKEN and the train would never fire (gh-2026). Unset every
# extraheader key the same way the runner's post-job cleanup does.
while IFS= read -r extraheader_key; do
  [ -n "$extraheader_key" ] || continue
  git config --local --unset-all "$extraheader_key" || true
done < <(git config --local --name-only --get-regexp 'http\..*\.extraheader' 2>/dev/null || true)

target="${RELEASE_TARGET_SHA:-${GITHUB_SHA:?}}"
echo "tag $tag missing — minting annotated tag at $target (token-URL push, fires the tag train)"
git fetch origin "$target" --depth=1 2>/dev/null || git fetch origin main --depth=50
# CI checkout carries no identity; annotate as the actions bot without
# touching global config (empty ident → exit 128, run 35426119831).
git -c user.name="github-actions[bot]" \
    -c user.email="41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com" \
    tag -a "$tag" -m "Release $tag" "$target"
# The push is NOT race-idempotent: tags never fast-forward, and the daily
# flow has up to ~5 parallel minters converging on the same missing tag
# (build-macos-cli's two arch legs plus build-extension and both attach
# legs). The loser's push is rejected ("already exists") — that is a WIN
# (a sibling leg minted the same commit), never a failure. Re-probe the
# ref before failing: present → continue to train verification; still
# absent → the push genuinely failed (credential, perms, incident) and
# the leg must go red with a self-explaining error.
if ! git push "${GH_TOKEN:+https://x-access-token:[REDACTED:Connection-String-Password]@github.com/${repo}.git}" "refs/tags/$tag"; then
  if git ls-remote --exit-code origin "refs/tags/$tag" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "tag $tag was minted concurrently by a sibling leg — continuing to train verification"
  else
    echo "::error::tag $tag push failed and the ref is still missing — the push itself failed (credential, permissions, or a GitHub incident), not a race with a sibling leg. No draft will be created; fix the push and re-run." >&2
    exit 1
  fi
fi

# Guard 2 — the train must actually start. A push that fires no workflow
# run (a GITHUB_TOKEN-classed credential on the wire, a GitHub incident, a
# workflow-file mismatch at the tag commit) silently strands every draft
# attached to the tag: green legs, no publish, the sweeper cleans up a day
# later (v1.0.663 / v1.0.665). The run row for the push event appears
# within seconds; poll briefly and fail loud.
tries="${RELEASE_TRAIN_VERIFY_TRIES:-12}"
sleep_s="${RELEASE_TRAIN_VERIFY_SLEEP:-10}"
runs_seen=0
for _ in $(seq 1 "$tries"); do
  sleep "$sleep_s"
  # A probe failure must NOT read as "no train": gh prefers GH_TOKEN (the
  # RELEASE_PAT) for this call, so a fine-grained PAT without Actions:read,
  # an expired PAT, or a rate limit all land here. Swallowing the error
  # (2>/dev/null || echo 0) burns the whole budget and then blames the push
  # credential — a misleading RCA on a red release leg. Fail fast and
  # surface the probe's own output instead.
  # gh can exit 0 yet write a warning to stderr (deprecation/upgrade
  # notice, config warning); merging stderr into the captured value would
  # corrupt the numeric check below ("integer expression expected") and
  # read as "no train" — rolling back a possibly-live tag over a benign
  # warning. Keep stderr OUT of the success value; surface it only on the
  # failure path.
  probe_err="$(mktemp)"
  probe_out="$(gh run list --repo "$repo" --branch "$tag" --limit 10 \
    --json databaseId --jq 'length' 2>"$probe_err")" || {
    echo "::error::train verification probe failed for $tag (gh run list): $(cat "$probe_err") — a failing probe (RELEASE_PAT without Actions:read, expired PAT, rate limit) is NOT evidence of a suppressed train; fix the probe credential before re-running." >&2
    rm -f "$probe_err"
    exit 1
  }
  rm -f "$probe_err"
  if [ "${probe_out:-0}" -gt 0 ]; then
    runs_seen=1
    break
  fi
done
if [ "$runs_seen" -ne 1 ]; then
  # Roll the untrained tag back before failing: the pushed ref left in
  # place would make the prescribed "fix the credential and re-run" skip
  # the mint (and its train check) entirely — the caller's plain
  # `gh release create --draft` would then attach a draft to a ref whose
  # train never ran, silently re-arming the exact stranded-draft shape
  # this script exists to prevent (v1.0.663 / v1.0.665). Drop the LOCAL
  # tag object too: a reused self-hosted workspace would otherwise die at
  # `git tag -a` on the re-run.
  echo "::warning::rolling back the untrained tag ref so a fixed re-run can re-mint" >&2
  git push "${GH_TOKEN:+https://x-access-token:[REDACTED:Connection-String-Password]@github.com/${repo}.git}" ":refs/tags/$tag" ||
    echo "::warning::rollback of refs/tags/$tag failed — a re-run will skip the mint (tag exists) and can strand the draft; delete refs/tags/$tag manually before re-running" >&2
  git tag -d "$tag" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  echo "::error::tag train did not start for $tag: pushed refs/tags/$tag to ${repo} but no workflow run appeared on the ref within the verification budget — the push likely authenticated as a CI-suppressed token (GitHub never fires workflows for GITHUB_TOKEN pushes; the persisted actions/checkout extraheader must not outrank the GH_TOKEN push credentials), or the tag-trigger filter does not match. No draft was created; fix the push credential and re-run." >&2
  exit 1
fi
echo "✅ tag train for $tag started (workflow run visible on the ref) — the draft publish path is live"

#!/bin/bash
# Build a hardened-runtime, *non-sandboxed* macOS release of Fa.
# This flavor can spawn system interpreters (python3, bash, node, etc.)
# and is intended for GitHub Releases, not the App Store.
#
# Usage:
#   scripts/build_macos_nosandbox.sh
#
# Optional environment variables:
#   FA_CODE_SIGN_IDENTITY / MACOS_IDENTITY - signing identity.
#   FA_DEVELOPMENT_TEAM / MACOS_TEAM_ID     - Apple Team ID.
set -euo pipefail

cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."

# Prefer the new FA_* variables; fall back to the older MACOS_* names.
identity="${FA_CODE_SIGN_IDENTITY:-${MACOS_IDENTITY:--}}"
team="${FA_DEVELOPMENT_TEAM:-${MACOS_TEAM_ID:-}}"

# If no identity was requested, try to use a local Apple Development cert so
# the no-sandbox build still has a stable TeamIdentifier for TCC.
if [[ "$identity" == "-" ]]; then
  development_identity=$(security find-identity -v -p codesigning 2>/dev/null \
    | grep -m1 'Apple Development' \
    | sed -n 's/.*"\(.*\)".*/\1/p' || true)
  if [[ -n "$development_identity" ]]; then
    identity="Apple Development"
  fi
fi

# If we have a real identity but no team, extract the team identifier (OU)
# from the matching certificate's subject. HealthKit/HomeKit entitlements
# require a non-empty team.
if [[ "$identity" != "-" && -z "$team" ]]; then
  cert_label=$(security find-identity -v -p codesigning 2>/dev/null \
    | grep -F "$identity" \
    | head -n1 \
    | sed -n 's/.*"\(.*\)".*/\1/p' || true)
  if [[ -n "$cert_label" ]]; then
    team=$(security find-certificate -c "$cert_label" -p 2>/dev/null \
      | openssl x509 -noout -subject 2>/dev/null \
      | grep -oE 'OU=[A-Z0-9]+' \
      | cut -d= -f2 \
      | head -n1 || true)
  fi
fi

# Distribution/Developer ID certificates require manual signing; local
# Apple Development certificates use automatic signing.
if [[ "$identity" == "-" || "$identity" == "Apple Development" ]]; then
  export FA_CODE_SIGN_STYLE="${FA_CODE_SIGN_STYLE:-Automatic}"
else
  export FA_CODE_SIGN_STYLE="${FA_CODE_SIGN_STYLE:-Manual}"
fi

export FA_CODE_SIGN_IDENTITY="$identity"
export FA_DEVELOPMENT_TEAM="$team"
export FA_PROVISIONING_PROFILE_SPECIFIER="${FA_PROVISIONING_PROFILE_SPECIFIER:-}"

readonly APP="build/macos/Build/Products/Release/Fa.app"
readonly ENTITLEMENTS="macos/Runner/ReleaseNoSandbox.entitlements"

echo "[build_macos_nosandbox] Building Release (identity='${identity}', team='${team:-}')..."
flutter build macos --release

echo "[build_macos_nosandbox] Re-signing with no-sandbox entitlements..."
codesign --force \
  --deep \
  --sign "${identity}" \
  --entitlements "${ENTITLEMENTS}" \
  --options runtime \
  "${APP}"

echo "[build_macos_nosandbox] Entitlements now applied:"
codesign -d --entitlements - "${APP}" | grep -E 'app-sandbox|jit|personal-information|homekit|healthkit' || true

echo "[build_macos_nosandbox] Done: ${APP}"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Lazy DRAFT create for the release train's asset-upload steps (gh-1801).
#
# The train workflows (ci.yml binaries/web-spa, build-macos.yml
# build-macos-cli/build-extension) need a release object to attach assets
# to, but the release must never go live from an upload step: `fa update`
# resolves the `latest` release and hard-fails without the SIGNED
# SHA256SUMS(.sig) (bin/self_manage.dart provenance gate), which only the
# tag-run release-provenance job can upload. This script creates the
# release as a DRAFT — nothing else:
#
#   - body = scripts/release_notes.sh output (curated `## <version>`
#     CHANGELOG section → curated `## Unreleased` → conventional commits;
#     the gh-1172 curated-notes contract), with a minimal fallback —
#     never `--generate-notes` (review threads 3/7);
#   - body carries `<!-- release-draft-owner: run/<run_id>/job/<job> -->`
#     so scripts/release_draft_guard.sh can reclaim the draft on failure
#     (review threads 4/8) — matrix legs override the identity via
#     RELEASE_DRAFT_IDENTITY (e.g. binaries-linux-x64) so a failed leg's
#     guard can never match a sibling's in-flight draft;
#   - the view→create race is tolerated (`|| true`): a sibling leg or the
#     attach path may create the release between our view and create —
#     the loser just uploads into the winner's release;
#   - it NEVER publishes and NEVER flags latest: the single publish point
#     of a tag train is release-provenance's "Upload provenance assets"
#     step (`gh release edit --draft=false --latest` after SHA256SUMS.sig
#     lands). A red provenance leaves the previous release as latest —
#     safe degradation, never a provenance-less latest (v1.0.630 window).
#
# Usage: release_lazy_draft.sh <tag>
# Env: GITHUB_REPOSITORY, GITHUB_RUN_ID, GITHUB_JOB (Actions defaults),
#      RELEASE_DRAFT_IDENTITY (optional leg-suffixed override),
#      GH_TOKEN/GITHUB_TOKEN.
set -euo pipefail

tag="${1:?usage: release_lazy_draft.sh <tag>}"
repo="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY:?GITHUB_REPOSITORY must be set}"
identity="${RELEASE_DRAFT_IDENTITY:-run/${GITHUB_RUN_ID:?GITHUB_RUN_ID must be set (GitHub Actions default env)}/job/${GITHUB_JOB:?GITHUB_JOB must be set (GitHub Actions default env)}}"

# The guard greps exactly this class — validate here so a malformed
# override fails loud instead of stamping a marker the guard could never
# match (a forever-orphaned draft).
printf '%s' "$identity" | grep -Eq '^run/[0-9]+/job/[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$' || {
  echo "::error::RELEASE_DRAFT_IDENTITY '$identity' does not match 'run/<id>/job/<name>' — the draft lifecycle guard could never reclaim such a draft" >&2
  exit 1
}

# Already created (by a sibling leg, the attach path, or a previous run)?
# Drafts and published releases both resolve here — upload-only is safe.
if gh release view "$tag" --repo "$repo" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "release $tag already exists — lazy draft create skipped"
  exit 0
fi

# Body: curated notes (CHANGELOG section / Unreleased / conventional
# commits) plus the ownership marker the guard verifies before deleting.
# stderr is NOT swallowed: release_notes.sh's ::error gates (e.g. the
# duplicate-'## Unreleased' curation guard) must stay visible even when
# the minimal fallback below keeps the train moving.
notes_file="$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/release-lazy-notes.XXXXXX")"
trap 'rm -f "$notes_file"' EXIT
if ! bash "$(dirname "$0")/release_notes.sh" "$tag" >"$notes_file" ||
  [ ! -s "$notes_file" ]; then
  printf 'Release %s — see the CHANGELOG.\n' "$tag" >"$notes_file"
fi
marker="<!-- release-draft-owner: $identity -->"
grep -qF "$marker" "$notes_file" || printf '\n%s\n' "$marker" >>"$notes_file"

# gh-2026: a `gh release create` for a MISSING ref REST-mints a
# lightweight API tag with NO push event — the v0.1.408 silent class
# (issue #597). The fast legs (build-macos.yml build-extension /
# build-macos-cli) can reach this create before the attach legs
# (release-macos / release-mobile): the silent mint wins the race, every
# attach leg then finds the tag existing and skips the CI-firing
# annotated push, no tag train ever runs, and the draft is stranded
# (swept a day later — the v1.0.663 / v1.0.665 shape). When the ref is
# DEFINITELY missing, mint it through the CI-firing annotated push and
# verify the train started BEFORE creating the draft (dispatch-time call
# sites export GH_TOKEN=RELEASE_PAT for exactly this; the ci.yml tag-run
# call sites always see the tag of their own push event and never enter
# the mint). An indeterminable verdict (no origin remote, rc 128 —
# sandboxed fixtures) falls through to the plain create path.
set +e
git ls-remote --exit-code origin "refs/tags/$tag" >/dev/null 2>&1
ls_remote_rc=$?
set -e
if [ "$ls_remote_rc" -eq 2 ]; then
  bash "$(dirname "$0")/release_tag_mint.sh" "$tag"
fi

# DRAFT-first (gh-1801): a create here must never publish — the resolved
# asset list at this point can never include the signed checksums. The
# race-lost create is tolerated (the winner owns the release).
gh release create "$tag" \
  --repo "$repo" \
  --title "$tag" \
  --draft \
  --notes-file "$notes_file" || true
echo "✅ lazy draft ready for $tag (owner $identity) — publish is provenance-owned (gh-1801)"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# ci-sign — host-level signing mediator for self-hosted macOS runners.
#
# WHY THIS EXISTS (gh-1865 / gh-1866, owner decision 2026-10-28)
#
# The fa-m5 pool is ONE Mac under ONE user account hosting several runner
# registrations (fa-m5-1/2/3, plus the yoloit / learn.ai / yoclip runners).
# Every signing job used to create its OWN temporary keychain and publish it
# through the PER-USER GLOBAL keychain search list. Two failure classes came
# out of that:
#
#   1. Eviction (gh-1866, runs 40165497544 → 40165498619): a fixed-list
#      writer replaced the whole search list and evicted a concurrent job's
#      keychain → "No certificate for team ... found".
#   2. Ambiguity (gh-1865, run 40455401630): the additive union helper fixed
#      (1) but left TWO same-subject certificates ("Apple Distribution:
#      Uladzimir Klyshevich (YP9HC3USZ3)", different serials — the iOS and
#      the macOS distribution certs) in one list; xcodebuild resolved the
#      generic name to the WRONG cert and the iOS archive died after ~24 min
#      ("Provisioning profile doesn't include signing certificate").
#   3. Interactive GUI keychain-password prompts on the owner's desktop:
#      runners live in the user's Aqua launchd session, and a leftover or
#      locked per-job keychain (empty password) makes SecurityAgent pop a
#      dialog mid-CI.
#
# THE MODEL: ONE persistent per-host keychain (ci-signing.keychain-db),
# provisioned ONCE and idempotently re-verified, holding every distribution
# identity. Signing jobs NEVER create or delete keychains and NEVER write
# the search list for signing purposes. Identity resolution is pinned by
# SHA-1 everywhere (xcodebuild CODE_SIGN_IDENTITY / codesign -s SHA1
# --keychain), so same-named certificates can coexist and legs stay
# parallel. `doctor` fail-fasts on profile/identity mismatches in seconds
# instead of after a dead archive.
#
# USAGE
#   ci-sign install <label>            import/refresh identity from env
#       reads CI_SIGN_<LABEL>_P12_B64 + CI_SIGN_<LABEL>_P12_PASSWORD, or
#       CI_SIGN_P12_B64_ENV / CI_SIGN_P12_PASSWORD_ENV naming the env vars
#       that hold them (legacy workflow secret names). Idempotent: a
#       re-run with the SAME certificate is a no-op; a DIFFERENT cert
#       replaces the previous one for the label. --force re-imports even
#       if the fingerprint matches.
#   ci-sign sha1 <label>               print the pinned SHA-1 fingerprint
#   ci-sign serial <label>             print the certificate serial (hex)
#   ci-sign name <label>               print the certificate common name
#   ci-sign codesign <label> [args…]   exec codesign --keychain <kc> -s <SHA1> args…
#   ci-sign doctor <profile>[ <label>] fail fast: every cert embedded in the
#                                      provisioning profile must match an
#                                      identity in the signing keychain
#   ci-sign unlock                     unlock the keychain non-interactively
#   ci-sign list                       list valid codesigning identities
#   ci-sign cleanup-legacy             best-effort delete known per-job
#                                      keychains left by older workflows
#   ci-sign path                       print the keychain path
#
# EXIT CODES: 0 ok; 1 operational failure (mismatch, missing identity);
# 2 usage error. When GITHUB_ACTIONS is set, failures emit ::error lines.
set -euo pipefail

# The keychain path is overridable for tests (CI_SIGN_KEYCHAIN) — the
# default is the persistent host keychain. CI_SIGN_KEYCHAIN_PASSWORD
# already overrides the stored password the same way.
KC="${CI_SIGN_KEYCHAIN:-$HOME/Library/Keychains/ci-signing.keychain-db}"
CFG="$HOME/.config/ci-sign"
KCPASS_FILE="$CFG/keychain-password"
LABELS_DIR="$CFG/labels"

err() { if [ -n "${GITHUB_ACTIONS:-}" ]; then echo "::error::ci-sign: $*" >&2; else echo "ci-sign: $*" >&2; fi; }
die() { err "$*"; exit 1; }
usage() { echo "usage: ci-sign <install|sha1|serial|name|codesign|doctor|unlock|list|cleanup-legacy|path> ..." >&2; exit 2; }

[ $# -ge 1 ] || usage
CMD="$1"; shift

kc_password() {
  # Keychain password: [REDACTED:Sensitive-Value] if provided, else a stored
  # random one (created on first use). 0600 user-only file — it protects a
  # CI-only keychain whose certificates are already provisioned from repo
  # secrets by a trusted workflow.
  if [ -n "${CI_SIGN_KEYCHAIN_PASSWORD:-}" ]; then
    printf '%s' "$CI_SIGN_KEYCHAIN_PASSWORD"
    return 0
  fi
  if [ ! -s "$KCPASS_FILE" ]; then
    mkdir -p "$CFG"
    umask 077
    openssl rand -base64 32 > "$KCPASS_FILE"
  fi
  cat "$KCPASS_FILE"
}

ensure_keychain() {
  local kcpass
  kcpass="$(kc_password)"
  if [ ! -f "$KC" ]; then
    mkdir -p "$CFG"
    security create-keychain -p "$kcpass" "$KC"
  fi

  # (lock on sleep + 24h backstop) assumed "every ci-sign entry point
  # unlocks anyway" — but gym's `xcodebuild -showBuildSettings` is NOT a
  # ci-sign entry point: it runs ~15 min after the unlock and hit a locked
  # keychain's GUI password prompt on the headless runner (4 retries,
  # fastlane timeout, run 40849468765). Settings only apply
  # non-interactively on a FRESH keychain; on an existing one the command

  # applied non-interactively on an existing keychain anyway (see the
  # gh-1963 notes) and never provided anti-lock: that job belongs to the
  # point-of-use unlocks + the Fastfile unlock watchdog (gh-1965).
  security unlock-keychain -p "$kcpass" "$KC"
  # Idempotent, additive, self-verifying search-list membership (gh-1866
  # logic, applied ONCE for a persistent entry — never per job). Skipped
  # for test keychains (CI_SIGN_KEYCHAIN override) — they never leave the
  # test sandbox.

# produced a garbled list (System duplicated, login.keychain-db missing,
  # default dangling → "A keychain cannot be found to store" GUI dialogs
  # and gh auth failures on the shared host). Dedupe, keep login FIRST,
  # append ci-signing LAST, always write the full explicit list.
  if [ -z "${CI_SIGN_KEYCHAIN:-}" ]; then
    local rest login_kc
    login_kc="$HOME/Library/Keychains/login.keychain-db"
    rest="$(security list-keychains | sed 's/[[:space:]]//g; s/"//g' | grep -v '^$' | grep -vxF "$KC" | grep -vxF "$login_kc" | awk '!seen[$0]++')"
    if [ -f "$login_kc" ]; then
      security list-keychains -d user -s "$login_kc" $rest "$KC"
    else
      security list-keychains -d user -s $rest "$KC"
    fi
    security list-keychains | sed 's/[[:space:]]//g; s/"//g' | grep -qxF "$KC" || die "failed to add keychain to search list"
  fi
}

do_unlock() {
  [ -f "$KC" ] || die "no signing keychain at $KC — run 'ci-sign install <label>' first (host provisioning)"
  security unlock-keychain -p "$(kc_password)" "$KC"
}

p12_env_value() { # p12_env_value <VARNAME>
  local var="$1"
  [ -n "${!var:-}" ] || die "env $var is not set"
  printf '%s' "${!var}"
}

label_env() { # label_env <label> <SUFFIX> -> prints resolved env var VALUE
  local label="$1" suffix="$2"
  local upper="${label^^}"
  upper="${upper//-/_}"
  if [ -n "${CI_SIGN_P12_B64_ENV:-}" ] || [ -n "${CI_SIGN_P12_PASSWORD_ENV:-}" ]; then
    # Legacy secret names, mapped explicitly by the caller.
    case "$suffix" in
      P12_B64)      [ -n "${CI_SIGN_P12_B64_ENV:-}" ]      && p12_env_value "$CI_SIGN_P12_B64_ENV"      && return 0 ;;
      P12_PASSWORD) [ -n "${CI_SIGN_P12_PASSWORD_ENV:-}" ] && p12_env_value "$CI_SIGN_P12_PASSWORD_ENV" && return 0 ;;
    esac
  fi
  p12_env_value "CI_SIGN_${upper}_${suffix}"
}

# gh-1954: OpenSSL 3.x refuses RC2-40-CBC-encrypted P12 payloads without
# the legacy provider ("inner_evp_generic_fetch:unsupported ... Algorithm
# (RC2-40-CBC : 0)", run 40840166571 probe). Older Apple distribution
# exports use exactly RC2-40-CBC; the pre-v3 pipeline never noticed because
# security(1) handles RC2 natively. LibreSSL does not know -legacy — add it
# only for OpenSSL 3.x.
OSS_LEGACY=""
case "$(openssl version 2>/dev/null)" in
  OpenSSL\ 3*) OSS_LEGACY="-legacy";;
esac

import_fingerprint() { # import_fingerprint <p12file> <password>; prints SHA1 (no colons)
  local tmp
  tmp="$(mktemp -d)"
  # shellcheck disable=SC2064
  trap "rm -rf '$tmp'" RETURN
  # gh-1954 signature B: when the payload cannot be read, the previous
  # "cannot read P12" gave zero diagnostics. Log the openssl error and
  # the payload shape (both non-secret) so the failure is actionable.
  if ! openssl pkcs12 $OSS_LEGACY -passin "pass:$2" -in "$1" -clcerts -nokeys -out "$tmp/c.pem" 2>"$tmp/err1"; then
    if ! openssl pkcs12 $OSS_LEGACY -passin "pass:" -in "$1" -clcerts -nokeys -out "$tmp/c.pem" 2>"$tmp/err2"; then
      err "pkcs12 with secret password: $(tail -2 "$tmp/err1" | tr '\n' ' ')"
      err "pkcs12 with empty password:  $(tail -2 "$tmp/err2" | tr '\n' ' ')"
      err "payload: $(wc -c < "$1" | tr -d ' ') bytes, head: $(head -c 24 "$1" | od -An -tx1 | tr -s ' ' | cut -c1-40)"
      if head -c 11 "$1" | grep -q -- '-----BEGIN'; then
        err "payload looks like PEM TEXT, not a binary PKCS12 — the secret may hold base64-of-PEM (cert only), not base64-of-p12"
      fi
      return 1
    fi
  fi
  openssl x509 -in "$tmp/c.pem" -noout -fingerprint -sha1 2>/dev/null \
    | sed 's/^.*=//; s/://g'
}

verify_label_identity() { # verify_label_identity <label>; echoes sha1
  local label="$1"
  local mf="$LABELS_DIR/$label"
  local sha1
  [ -f "$mf" ] || die "label '$label' is not provisioned (no $mf) — run 'ci-sign install $label' first (host provisioning)"
  sha1="$(sed -n 's/^sha1=//p' "$mf")"
  [ -n "$sha1" ] || die "corrupt manifest for '$label'"
  do_unlock
  if ! security find-identity -v "$KC" | grep -qi "$sha1"; then
    die "identity $sha1 (label '$label') is not a VALID codesigning identity in the signing keychain — re-run 'ci-sign install $label --force'"
  fi
  printf '%s' "$sha1"
}

case "$CMD" in
  path)
    echo "$KC"
    ;;

  unlock)
    do_unlock
    echo "unlocked $KC"
    ;;

  list)

    ;;

  install)
    LABEL="${1:-}"; [ -n "$LABEL" ] || usage
    # Labels become file paths under $LABELS_DIR — refuse anything that
    # could escape it (../foo, a/b, empty).
    case "$LABEL" in
      ''|*[!A-Za-z0-9_-]*) die "invalid label '$LABEL' (allowed: [A-Za-z0-9_-])" ;;
    esac
    FORCE=0; [ "${2:-}" = "--force" ] && FORCE=1
    # Concurrent installs (two matrix legs re-verifying on the same host)
    # serialize on a lock dir — create-keychain/import are not idempotent
    # under race; the happy path after first provisioning is a no-op that
    # holds the lock for milliseconds.
    LOCK="$CFG/install.lock"
    mkdir -p "$CFG"
    ACQUIRED=0
    # gh-1964: wait up to 600s (was 120s) — a real re-import on the shared
    # host takes ~2 min; concurrent waves (provision + build) must
    # serialize by WAITING, not by failing the later wave (run 40857285170).
    for _ in $(seq 1 300); do
      if mkdir "$LOCK" 2>/dev/null; then ACQUIRED=1; break; fi
      # Stale-lock recovery: a SIGKILLed holder would wedge host signing
      # forever. The happy path holds the lock for seconds; a lock older
      # than 30 min cannot be alive — steal it.
      if [ -d "$LOCK" ]; then
        LOCK_AGE=$(( $(date +%s) - $(stat -f %m "$LOCK" 2>/dev/null || echo 0) ))
        if [ "$LOCK_AGE" -gt 1800 ]; then
          err "stealing stale install lock (age ${LOCK_AGE}s > 1800s)"
          rmdir "$LOCK" 2>/dev/null || true
        fi
      fi
      sleep 2
    done
    [ "$ACQUIRED" -eq 1 ] || die "another ci-sign install holds the lock ($LOCK)"
    trap 'rmdir "$LOCK" 2>/dev/null || true' EXIT
    P12_B64="$(label_env "$LABEL" P12_B64)"
    P12_PW="$(label_env "$LABEL" P12_PASSWORD)"
    [ -n "$P12_B64" ] || die "empty P12 payload for label '$LABEL'"

    if [ "$FORCE" = "1" ] && [ -f "$KC" ]; then
      # gh-1954: --force recreates the keychain from scratch — the only
      # non-interactive way to change keychain settings (auto-lock) on an
      # existing keychain is impossible (GUI prompt); a fresh keychain
      # accepts set-keychain-settings right after create-keychain. The
      # identity is re-imported from the repo-secret P12 below.
      err "--force: deleting existing keychain $KC for fresh re-provision"
      security delete-keychain "$KC" 2>/dev/null || rm -f "$KC"
    fi
    ensure_keychain
    TMP="$(mktemp -d)"
    # One consolidated EXIT trap (a second `trap ... EXIT` would REPLACE
    # the lock-release trap above, leaking the lock dir).
    trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"; rmdir "$LOCK" 2>/dev/null || true' EXIT
    printf '%s' "$P12_B64" | base64 --decode > "$TMP/cert.p12" 2>/dev/null || die "P12 payload for '$LABEL' is not valid base64"

    NEW_FP="$(import_fingerprint "$TMP/cert.p12" "$P12_PW")" || die "cannot read P12 for '$LABEL' (wrong password or corrupt payload?)"
    if [ -z "$NEW_FP" ]; then
      err "pkcs12 parsed but NO client certificate extracted — payload diagnostics:"
      err "  size: $(wc -c < "$TMP/cert.p12" | tr -d ' ') bytes"
      err "  first bytes: $(head -c 24 "$TMP/cert.p12" | od -An -tx1 | tr -s ' ' | cut -c1-48)"
      if head -c 11 "$TMP/cert.p12" | grep -q -- '-----BEGIN'; then
        err "  payload is PEM TEXT (base64-of-PEM in the secret, not base64-of-p12!)"
      fi
      err "  pkcs12 cert inventory: $(openssl pkcs12 $OSS_LEGACY -passin "pass:$P12_PW" -in "$TMP/cert.p12" -nokeys 2>&1 | grep -cE 'subject=[REDACTED:Certificate-DN]
      err "  pkcs12 no-cert probe: $(openssl pkcs12 $OSS_LEGACY -passin "pass:$P12_PW" -in "$TMP/cert.p12" -nocerts -nodes 2>&1 | tail -1 || true)"
      die "cannot read P12 for '$LABEL' (parsed but no client certificate)"
    fi

    OLD_FP="$( [ -f "$LABELS_DIR/$LABEL" ] && sed -n 's/^sha1=//p' "$LABELS_DIR/$LABEL" || true )"
    if [ "$FORCE" -eq 0 ] && [ "$NEW_FP" = "$OLD_FP" ]; then

# fa-macos, fa-macos-installer) — an identity is a shadow ONLY if
        # no label manifest in $LABELS_DIR pins its SHA-1. The #2009 form
        # ("not the current label pin") deleted the other labels' live
        # identities (run 41276487426 arm64 attempt 2), and its echo died
        # under set -u on a never-assigned variable in the echo.
        ALL_PINNED="$(sed -n 's/^sha1=//p' "$LABELS_DIR"/* 2>/dev/null | tr 'a-f' 'A-F')"
        for FP in $(security find-identity -v -p codesigning "$KC" | sed -n 's/^ *[0-9]*) \([0-9A-F]\{40\}\) .*/\1/p'); do
          if [ "$FP" != "$NEW_FP" ] && ! printf '%s\n' "$ALL_PINNED" | grep -qxF "$FP"; then
            security delete-identity -Z "$FP" "$KC" 2>/dev/null \
              || err "could not remove shadow identity $FP (continuing)"
            echo "ci-sign: swept shadow identity $FP from '$(basename "$KC")'"
          fi
        done
        echo "ci-sign: identity for '$LABEL' is up to date ($NEW_FP)"
        exit 0
      fi
      echo "ci-sign: manifest matches but identity invalid — re-importing"
    fi

    if [ -n "$OLD_FP" ] && [ "$OLD_FP" != "$NEW_FP" ]; then
      security delete-identity -Z "$OLD_FP" "$KC" 2>/dev/null \
        || err "could not remove previous identity $OLD_FP for '$LABEL' (continuing; stale identity remains)"
    fi

    # gh-1954: unlock BEFORE import — a locked (freshly recreated)
    # keychain makes security import raise a GUI password prompt; on the
    # headless runner that hangs, and a user Cancel aborts the import
    # ("SecKeychainItemImport: User canceled the operation", run
    # 40857357741). unlock-keychain -p never prompts.
    security unlock-keychain -p "$(kc_password)" "$KC"
    # gh-2026: -T grants import-time key ACL per consumer binary. codesign alone
    # is NOT enough — productbuild (TestFlight PKG) is not covered by the
    # apple-tool:/apple: partition list and its first signing raised a modal
    # SecurityAgent dialog that hung the arm64 leg 1h42m (run 41354303751).
    security import "$TMP/cert.p12" -k "$KC" -P "$P12_PW" \
      -T /usr/bin/codesign -T /usr/bin/productbuild \
      -T /usr/bin/productsign -T /usr/bin/security
    # Partition the private key so codesign never needs interactive auth
    # (this is what prevents GUI keychain prompts).
    # applied twice: the first apply does not always stick on a fresh
    # import (fastlane folklore, cheap and harmless).
    security set-key-partition-list -S apple-tool:,apple: -s -k "$(kc_password)" "$KC" >/dev/null
    security set-key-partition-list -S apple-tool:,apple: -s -k "$(kc_password)" "$KC" >/dev/null

    if ! security find-identity -v "$KC" | grep -qi "$NEW_FP"; then
      die "imported P12 for '$LABEL' but it is not a valid codesigning identity (expired, revoked, or key/cert mismatch). Try 'ci-sign install $LABEL --force', then check the certificate in Apple Developer Portal."
    fi

    mkdir -p "$LABELS_DIR"
    CERT_PEM="$TMP/c.pem"
    openssl pkcs12 $OSS_LEGACY -passin "pass:$P12_PW" -in "$TMP/cert.p12" -clcerts -nokeys -out "$CERT_PEM" 2>/dev/null \
      || openssl pkcs12 $OSS_LEGACY -passin "pass:" -in "$TMP/cert.p12" -clcerts -nokeys -out "$CERT_PEM" 2>/dev/null || true
    SERIAL="$(openssl x509 -in "$CERT_PEM" -noout -serial | sed 's/^serial=//')"
    NAME="$(openssl x509 -in "$CERT_PEM" -noout -subject -nameopt multiline 2>/dev/null | sed -n 's/.*commonName[^:]*://p' | head -1)"
    umask 077
    { echo "sha1=$NEW_FP"; echo "serial=$SERIAL"; echo "name=$NAME"; echo "updated=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)"; } > "$LABELS_DIR/$LABEL"

    echo "ci-sign: installed identity for '$LABEL': $NAME"
    echo "  sha1=$NEW_FP serial=$SERIAL"
    ;;

  sha1|serial|name)
    LABEL="${1:-}"; [ -n "$LABEL" ] || usage
    MF="$LABELS_DIR/$LABEL"
    case "$CMD" in
      sha1)   verify_label_identity "$LABEL"; echo ;;
      serial) sed -n 's/^serial=//p' "$MF" ;;
      name)   sed -n 's/^name=//p' "$MF" ;;
    esac
    ;;

  codesign)
    LABEL="${1:-}"; [ -n "$LABEL" ] || usage
    shift
    SHA1="$(verify_label_identity "$LABEL")"
    exec codesign --keychain "$KC" -s "$SHA1" "$@"
    ;;

  plist)
    # Decode a provisioning profile to a plist on stdout WITHOUT touching
    # keychain state: `security cms -D` requires a default keychain (none
    # exists on this host by design — default-keychain writes are part of
    # the old race), openssl cms does not.
    PROFILE="${1:-}"
    [ -n "$PROFILE" ] && [ -f "$PROFILE" ] || die "profile not found: ${PROFILE:-<none>}"
    openssl cms -inform DER -verify -noverify -in "$PROFILE" -out /dev/stdout 2>/dev/null
    ;;

  doctor)
    PROFILE="${1:-}"; LABEL="${2:-}"
    [ -n "$PROFILE" ] || usage
    [ -f "$PROFILE" ] || die "profile not found: $PROFILE"
    do_unlock

    # The extraction must fail CLEAN on garbage input (a traceback here is
    # exactly the "guard error" obscurity the precheck exists to avoid).
    PROFILE_SERIALS="$(python3 - "$PROFILE" <<'PYEOF'
import plistlib, subprocess, sys
try:
    raw = subprocess.run(["openssl", "cms", "-inform", "DER", "-verify", "-noverify",
                          "-in", sys.argv[1], "-out", "/dev/stdout"],
                         capture_output=True)
    d = plistlib.loads(raw.stdout)
except Exception:
    sys.exit(3)
for c in d.get("DeveloperCertificates", []):
    r = subprocess.run(["openssl", "x509", "-inform", "DER", "-noout", "-serial"],
                       input=c, capture_output=True)
    s = r.stdout.decode().strip()
    if s.startswith("serial="):
        print(s[len("serial="):])
PYEOF
)" || true
    [ -n "$PROFILE_SERIALS" ] || die "could not extract certificates from profile $PROFILE (not a valid mobileprovision?)"

    KC_SERIALS="$(security find-certificate -a -p "$KC" 2>/dev/null | python3 -c '
import sys, re, subprocess
pem = sys.stdin.read()
for m in re.finditer(r"[REDACTED:PEM-CERTIFICATE]", pem, re.S):
    r = subprocess.run(["openssl", "x509", "-noout", "-serial"], input=m.group(0).encode(), capture_output=True)
    s = r.stdout.decode().strip()
    if s.startswith("serial="):
        print(s[len("serial="):])
')"
    [ -n "$KC_SERIALS" ] || die "signing keychain has no readable identities — run 'ci-sign install <label>'"

    MISSING=0
    while IFS= read -r s; do
      [ -n "$s" ] || continue
      if ! printf '%s\n' "$KC_SERIALS" | grep -qxF "$s"; then
        err "profile $(basename "$PROFILE") embeds certificate serial $s which is NOT in the signing keychain — re-issue the profile under the current distribution certificate or run 'ci-sign install'"

content.thinking:
**CONFIRMED — root cause for Failure A is exactly this:**

actions/checkout **v7** changed credential persistence: the GITHUB_TOKEN extraheader (`http.https://github.com/.extraheader`) is NO LONGER written to the repo-LOCAL `.git/config`. Instead it is written to a **separate credentials config file** in RUNER_TEMP (`git-credentials-<uuid>.config`), and the repo-local config gets **`includeIf.gitdir:<gitdir>.path = <that file>`** entries pointing at it.

`release_tag_mint.sh` Guard 1 strips only repo-local extraheader keys:

```bash
git config --local --unset-all "$extraheader_key" || true
# from: git config --local --name-only --get-regexp 'http\..*\.extraheader'
``

With checkout v7:
- `git config --local --name-only --get-regexp 'http\..*\.extraheader'` — **the read DOES list the key** (git config reads merge all includes — the includeIf matches the repo gitdir, so the included credentials file is consulted).
- `git config --local --unset-all http.https://github.com/.extraheader` — **fails silently** (`|| true`): `--local` only writes/removes from `.git/config`, where the key does NOT exist (it's in the included file).

So after the strip, `git config http.https://github.com/.extraheader` STILL resolves (via includeIf) to `AUTHORIZATION: basic <base64 GITHUB_TOKEN>`. That header is added to every github.com HTTP request — and per the gh-2026 investigation, it outranks the URL-embedded `x-access-token:RELEASE_PAT` credentials. GitHub therefore classifies the push as a GITHUB_TOKEN push → NO tag-triggered workflow is created → the train verification finds nothing → the script rolls the tag back and fails loud. Exactly the observed failure.

Also note the observed push speed: mint push took 05:23:35.8 → 05:23:38.5 — consistent with a push that succeeded.

Wait, I should double-check the wire-precedence claim: does the extraheader actually outrank URL-embedded credentials? From the script's own docs (gh-2026): "actions/checkout had already persisted the JOB token in the repo-local git config as http.<host>/.extraheader = AUTHORIZATION: basic …. That header outranks the URL-embedded credentials on the wire, so GitHub saw a GITHUB_TOKEN push". That was the empirically proven premise that motivated the script. And v1.0.663/v1.0.65 failed exactly this way before the fix. So yes — established in-repo fact.

Hmm — but wait, one more check: in the pre-v7 failures (v1.0.663/65), the strip DIDN'T exist yet and the extraheader was in the local config. The gh-2026 fix added the strip and (presumably) trains started working — the v1.0.678/679/680/681 trains fired. Let me check: did any SUCCESSFUL mint go through release_tag_mint.sh since gh-2026 landed? The v1.0.681 train was cut by ci.yml's auto-release (App token on the runner — the release job). Hmm, the cli leg's mint path might not have run since gh-2026 (tags always pre-existing from auto_release). Actually the mint runs when the tag is missing at draft time. auto_release cuts tags on main pushes (2h coalesce) — so by the time the daily runs, the tag usually EXISTS (v1.0.681 existed). This leg minted v1.0.682 because auto_release hadn't cut it yet (last main push at ~00:22 → tag v1.0.681 at 01:02; main hasn't moved since, so v1.0.682 was never auto-cut; the daily cli leg derived next_tag=v1.0.682 and had to mint).

So THIS is the first real execution of the mint path since... whenever the tags started being pre-existing. And it exposed the checkout-v7 includeIf persistence gap.

Let me confirm WHEN checkout v7 got pinned (recently?) and whether previous successful mints ran under checkout v6. Let me find when the checkout pin was updated to v7.0.1 and whether release_tag_mint.sh ever succeeded end-to-end. Actually — simpler confirmation: the failure signature ALREADY names the extraheader class; my job is to prove the strip is ineffective under checkout v7 and fix it.

**The fix for release_tag_mint.sh**: strip the persisted credentials COMPLETELY:
1. Unset the `includeIf.gitdir:*.path` keys that point at `git-credentials-*.config` files in the repo-local config (exactly what checkout's own cleanup does: "Removing includeIf entries pointing to credentials config files" — matching `^includeIf\.gitdir:` and unsetting keys whose value paths are git-credentials-*.config files).
2. ALSO neutralize the credentials file itself (set the extraheader in the FILE to empty / remove the Authorization line), or simply remove the include entries — removing the includeIf keys in local config suffices (the file then isn't included; it may also be deleted like checkout does).

Look at checkout's own removeGitConfig/removeTokenConfig for the exact cleanup semantics — the cleanup code:

- `removeGitConfig(pattern, configKey, omitSubmodules?)` — for extraheader: `git config --local --name-only --get-regexp '${pattern}' && git config --local --unset-all '${configKey}' || :` per repo AND submodules.
- `removeIncludeIfEntries()` — lists `includeIf.gitdir:` keys, checks whether the VALUE path matches git-credentials-*.config, and removes those keys from local config.

Let me read that part of the TS to mirror it faithfully in the shell.
