content.text:
# gh-1865 model v3 (owner decision 2026-10-28) — host signing
# provisioning. Installs/refreshes the PERSISTENT host keychain
# (~/Library/Keychains/ci-signing.keychain-db) with every distribution
# identity the repo's signing legs need, and sweeps the per-job keychains
# left behind by the retired workflows (their orphans produced interactive
# SecurityAgent keychain-password prompts in the owner's GUI session).
#
# Dispatch-only by design: this touches persistent host state, never a
# push/schedule. Idempotent — re-running with the SAME certificates is a
# no-op; after a certificate rotation re-run installs the new serial and
# retires the old identity for the label.
#
# First run performs the actual provisioning; every signing workflow also
# re-verifies its label via `ci-sign install <label>` (a no-op when
# up-to-date), so a drift between host and repo self-heals on the next
# signing run.
name: Host signing provision (ci-sign)

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      force:
        description: 'Recreate signing keychains from scratch (gh-1954: applies never-auto-lock settings; re-imports identities from repo secrets)'
        type: boolean
        default: false

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  provision:
    name: Provision ci-sign host keychain
    # The keychain is HOST-global state (~/Library/Keychains/), and the
    # fa-m5 pool is three registrations on ONE host under ONE user — the
    # macos-m5 pool is correct routing (gh-1906: no workflow pins fa-m5-*
    # runner-NAME labels; a name label would silently match zero runners
    # and queue forever). Concurrent provisioning across registrations is
    # safe: ci-sign install is idempotent and serializes on its lock dir.
    runs-on: [self-hosted, macos-m5]
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Install ci-sign onto the host PATH
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          mkdir -p "$HOME/bin"
          cp scripts/ci-sign "$HOME/bin/ci-sign"
          chmod +x "$HOME/bin/ci-sign"
          "$HOME/bin/ci-sign" path

      - name: Provision iOS distribution identity
        env:
          IOS_P12_BASE64: ${{ secrets.IOS_P12_BASE64 }}
          IOS_P12_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.IOS_P12_PASSWORD }}
          CI_SIGN_P12_B64_ENV: IOS_P12_BASE64
          CI_SIGN_P12_PASSWORD_ENV: IOS_P12_PASSWORD
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if [ -z "${IOS_P12_BASE64:-}" ]; then
            echo "::warning::IOS_P12_BASE64 not set — iOS label not provisioned"
            exit 0
          fi
          if [ "${{ inputs.force }}" = "true" ]; then
            ~/bin/ci-sign install fa-ios --force
          else
            ~/bin/ci-sign install fa-ios
          fi
          echo "ios sha1=$(~/bin/ci-sign sha1 fa-ios) serial=$(~/bin/ci-sign serial fa-ios) name=$(~/bin/ci-sign name fa-ios)"

      - name: Provision macOS distribution identity
        env:
          MACOS_CERTIFICATE_P12_BASE64: ${{ secrets.MACOS_CERTIFICATE_P12_BASE64 }}
          MACOS_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.MACOS_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD }}
          CI_SIGN_P12_B64_ENV: MACOS_CERTIFICATE_P12_BASE64
          CI_SIGN_P12_PASSWORD_ENV: MACOS_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if [ -z "${MACOS_CERTIFICATE_P12_BASE64:-}" ]; then
            echo "::warning::MACOS_CERTIFICATE_P12_BASE64 not set — macOS label not provisioned"
            exit 0
          fi
          ~/bin/ci-sign install fa-macos
          echo "macos sha1=$(~/bin/ci-sign sha1 fa-macos) serial=$(~/bin/ci-sign serial fa-macos) name=$(~/bin/ci-sign name fa-macos)"

      - name: Provision macOS installer identity
        env:
          MACOS_INSTALLER_P12_BASE64: ${{ secrets.MACOS_INSTALLER_P12_BASE64 }}
          MACOS_INSTALLER_P12_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.MACOS_INSTALLER_P12_PASSWORD }}
          CI_SIGN_P12_B64_ENV: MACOS_INSTALLER_P12_BASE64
          CI_SIGN_P12_PASSWORD_ENV: MACOS_INSTALLER_P12_PASSWORD
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if [ -z "${MACOS_INSTALLER_P12_BASE64:-}" ]; then
            echo "::notice::MACOS_INSTALLER_P12_BASE64 not set — macos-installer label not provisioned (TestFlight PKG leg skips itself)"
            exit 0
          fi
          ~/bin/ci-sign install fa-macos-installer
          echo "macos-installer sha1=$(~/bin/ci-sign sha1 fa-macos-installer) serial=$(~/bin/ci-sign serial fa-macos-installer)"

      - name: Sweep legacy per-job keychains
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          ~/bin/ci-sign cleanup-legacy
          echo "--- final state ---"
          ~/bin/ci-sign list

- name: Package TestFlight PKG (arm64)
        if: matrix.arch == 'arm64'
        id: testflight_pkg
        env:
          MACOS_INSTALLER_P12_BASE64: ${{ secrets.MACOS_INSTALLER_P12_BASE64 }}
          MACOS_INSTALLER_P12_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.MACOS_INSTALLER_P12_PASSWORD }}
          CI_SIGN_P12_B64_ENV: MACOS_INSTALLER_P12_BASE64
          CI_SIGN_P12_PASSWORD_ENV: MACOS_INSTALLER_P12_PASSWORD
          MACOS_INSTALLER_CERT_ID: ${{ secrets.MACOS_INSTALLER_CERT_ID }}
          VERSION: ${{ needs.version.outputs.version }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if [ -z "${MACOS_INSTALLER_P12_BASE64:-}" ]; then
            echo "::notice::Mac Installer Distribution cert not configured — skipping TestFlight PKG (the DMG path is unaffected)."
            exit 0
          fi
          # gh-1865 model v3: the installer cert lives in the PERSISTENT
          # ci-signing keychain under its own label (idempotent install —
          # the old lazy keychain re-create + search-list re-assert here
          # was gh-1866 exposure #2). productbuild signs by the SHA-1
          # fingerprint, immune to same-subject name shadowing.
          ~/bin/ci-sign install fa-macos-installer
          INSTALLER_SHA1=$(~/bin/ci-sign sha1 fa-macos-installer)

          APP_PATH="flutter_app/build/macos/Build/Products/Release/Fa.app"
          PKG_NAME="fa-macos-arm64-${VERSION}.pkg"
          echo "Building TestFlight package: $APP_PATH → $PKG_NAME"
          productbuild --component "$APP_PATH" /Applications "$PKG_NAME" \
            --sign "$INSTALLER_SHA1"
          echo "pkg_name=$PKG_NAME" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT

      - name: Notarize DMG
        if: steps.signing.outputs.signed == 'true'
        env:
          MACOS_NOTARIZE_APPLE_ID: ${{ secrets.MACOS_NOTARIZE_APPLE_ID }}
          MACOS_NOTARIZE_TEAM_ID: ${{ secrets.MACOS_NOTARIZE_TEAM_ID }}
          MACOS_NOTARIZE_APP_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.MACOS_NOTARIZE_APP_PASSWORD }}
          DMG_NAME: ${{ steps.package.outputs.dmg_name }}
        run: |
          if [ -z "$MACOS_NOTARIZE_APPLE_ID" ]; then
            echo "⚠️  Notarization secrets not set — skipping notarization"
            exit 0
          fi
          echo "Submitting for notarization..."
          xcrun notarytool submit "$DMG_NAME" \
            --apple-id "$MACOS_NOTARIZE_APPLE_ID" \
            --team-id "$MACOS_NOTARIZE_TEAM_ID" \
            --password "$MACOS_NOTARIZE_APP_PASSWORD" \
            --wait
          xcrun stapler staple "$DMG_NAME"
          echo "✅ Notarization complete"

      - name: Submit PKG to TestFlight

Wait — that step is `if: matrix.arch == 'arm64'` — so it did NOT run in the x86_64 leg. Hmm. And the arm64 leg ran it at ~06:00 (before its no-sandbox? no wait — the arm64 step order: ... "Package TestFlight PKG (arm64)" (953) comes BEFORE "Notarize DMG" (984), "Upload TestFlight PKG artifact" (1032), "Upload macOS artifacts" (1040), "Build and package no-sandbox release" (1050). So in the ARM64 leg (which succeeded fully), the order was: sandboxed build → DMG → TestFlight PKG (`ci-sign install fa-macos-installer` — a SECOND identity import!) → notarize → no-sandbox build (SUCCEEDED ~06:0x).

Hmm wait, when exactly did arm64's steps run? arm64 job: 05:22:01 → 06:03:37. Its no-sandbox build finished by 06:03:37. Its TestFlight PKG ran somewhere ~05:5x. The `ci-sign install fa-macos-installer` in the arm64 leg: NEW_FP = installer cert. OLD_FP = manifest value. If they match → happy path + SHADOW SWEEP. The shadow sweep deletes identities NOT pinned by any label manifest...

**AND HERE IT IS:** the shadow sweep! Look at the sweep logic again:

```bash
ALL_PINED="$(sed -n 's/^sha1=//p' "$LABELS_DIR"/* 2>/dev/null | tr 'a-f' 'A-F')"
for FP in $(security find-identity -v -p codesigning "$KC" | sed -n 's/^ *[0-9]*) \([0-9A-F]\{40\}\) .*/\1/p'); do
 if [ "$FP" != "$NEW_FP" ] && ! printf '%s\n' "$ALL_PINED" | grep -qxF "$FP"; then
   security delete-identity -Z "$FP" "$KC" ...
``

`security find-identity -v -p codesigning` lists VALID identities. The sweep deletes only unpinned ones. fa-macos's 43AEC... is pinned (manifest written at import) → survives.

Hmm — wait, BUT: the arm64 leg's fa-macos-installer install — if the INSTALLER manifest did NOT exist yet (first import for that label), OLD_FP empty → goes the FULL IMPORT path (not happy path). The import path: `security import ... -T codesign -T productbuild...`, partition list, verify, write manifest. NO shadow sweep on the import path (the sweep is only on the happy path!). And no delete of fa-macos. OK.

So the arm64 leg at ~05:5x imported fa-macos-installer. Everything fine.

Now the x86_64 leg (06:03:41+): its provisioning at 06:07:37 says "identity for 'fa-macos' is up to date (43AEC...)". Note: the x86_64 leg's TestFlight PKG step is SKIPPED (arm64 only). Its no-sandbox build failed.

**So NOTHING in the x86_64 job deleted the identity... and nothing in-repo ran on the host between 06:27 (valid) and 06:34 (gone)?**

Hmm — wait, hold on. Let me reconsider. What ran on the HOST at 06:27-06:34? From the runs list (06:00-06:45 window): only ubuntu jobs (SM ticks, CI schedule at 06:40, dev gh-2039 at 06:42). The CI schedule run 41401439020 at 06:40:48 — after the failure. Nothing on the Mac.

So no CONCURRENT workflow deleted it. The deletion must have come from the x86_64 job's own processes OR the identity was NOT deleted but became UNAVAILABLE (locked keychain / search list).

Back to basics. What does the no-sandbox build do DIFFERENTLY in codesign terms?

1. The DMG step codesign calls run DIRECTLY in the job step (shell) — they inherit the job's environment.
2. The no-sandbox build runs `flutter build macos --release` → xcodebuild → xcode_backend.dart codesign — a CHILD PROCESS of the flutter tool.

"no identity found" — codesign's error when the identity isn't found in the SEARCHED keychains.

The build failed at `_embedAppFramework` → `_codesignFramework` — i.e., xcode_backend was EMBEDING (re-copying + re-signing) App.framework. This happens when the build decided to REBUILD/refresh the framework — because e.g. the pruned flutter_assets changed, or a version change (no --build-number passed this time → different FLUTER_BUILD_NUMBER/NAME → Xcode re-runs the embed phase!). 

The first flutter build (sandboxed, 06:07-06:27) used --build-name=1.0.682 --build-number=<run_number>. The no-sandbox build (06:29) runs WITHOUT --build-name/--build-number → pubspec's version (0.0.0-dev placeholder? or 1.0.682?) — the version job might set version in pubspec... either way DIFFERENT build settings → full embed phase re-runs → codesign App.framework/App.

Something changed on the host between 06:27:23 and 06:34:25 (or mid-build). Candidates:

This should keep it unlocked. UNLESS the keychain password is wrong for a REPLACED keychain file...

        ln = int.from_bytes(buf[i:i+nb], "big"); i += nb

Hmm wait, the positions: at 1503-157: "Apple Inc. / Apple Certification Authority / Apple Root CA" with dates 120405→270405. At 2531-2605: ANOTHER "Apple Root CA" with same dates (that's within the TSTInfo's certificate chain of the TSA?). At 263-2737: Apple Root CA AGAIN. So this single blob embeds Apple Root CA 3 times?? That's the structure of the main code signature CMS:

- The MAIN signedData: signer = Developer ID Application cert (Uladzimir), certificates = [signer, WWDR G2?]. 
- signerInfo unigned attribute: RFC3161 timestamp token = a NESTED signedData: signer = TSA cert (261030→261211), certificates = [TSA cert, ...].

But where's the Uladzimir signer cert?! The strings show NO "Uladzimir"/"Developer ID"/"WWDR" anywhere in this blob's printable strings — only Apple Root CA ×3, Apple Certification Authority ×3, TSA-ish dates.

CONCLUSION: The blob I extracted at 19618843 is ONLY the nested timestamp token (4283 bytes), not the main CMS. The main CMS is elsewhere in the SuperBlob — and my SuperBlob parsing failed (count garbage).

The interesting bit: even this nested token contains "Apple Root CA" certificates from the TSA — irrelevant.

The MAIN signature CMS: my OID search found only TWO signedData OIDs in the tail: 19614024 and 19618843. 19618843 = timestamp token (4283 bytes). 19614024 = ~4.8KB before it — hmm, that might be the MAIN CMS!! #!/usr/bin/env bash
# Mint a release tag as an ANNOTATED tag pushed with a CI-firing token, and
# verify the tag train actually started (gh-2026). Shared by the two
# draft-capable create paths:
#
#   - scripts/release_attach_or_create.sh (build-macos.yml release-macos,
#     build-mobile.yml release-mobile) — the tag was DEFINITELY missing at
#     attach time;
#   - scripts/release_lazy_draft.sh (build-macos.yml build-macos-cli /
#     build-extension) — a `gh release create` for a missing ref would
#     REST-mint a lightweight API tag with NO push event (the v0.1.408
#     silent class, issue #597): no tag train, a stranded draft.
#
# Why this exists — the v1.0.663 / v1.0.665 stale drafts (gh-2026): the
# release legs pushed the annotated tag through the GH_TOKEN URL, but
# actions/checkout had already persisted the JOB token in the repo-local
# git config as `http.<host>/.extraheader = AUTHORIZATION: basic …`. That
# header outranks the URL-embedded credentials on the wire, so GitHub saw
# a GITHUB_TOKEN push — and GitHub NEVER fires workflow runs for
# GITHUB_TOKEN pushes (gh-1172; docs/ci.md "its token triggers the
# tag-scoped jobs, which GITHUB_TOKEN pushes never do"). Both legs stayed
# green, no tag run ever existed on the refs, the provenance-owned publish
# (gh-1801) never ran, and the daily sweeper deleted the drafts a day
# later. Two guards close the class:
#
#   1. strip the persisted extraheader(s) before the push — the same
#      cleanup the Actions runner's post-job step performs ("Removing HTTP
#      extra header") — so the URL's PAT credentials are what GitHub sees
#      and the push fires ci.yml's `push: tags: ['v*']` train;
#   2. verify the outcome: poll for any workflow run on the tag ref within
#      a bounded budget. A push that triggers nothing fails this script
#      LOUD (no draft is created — the caller never reaches its create
#      step), so the leg goes red with a self-explaining error instead of
#      stranding a draft for the sweeper.
#
# Usage: release_tag_mint.sh <tag>
# Env: GITHUB_REPOSITORY, GITHUB_RUN_ID, GITHUB_JOB, GITHUB_SHA (Actions
#      defaults), GH_TOKEN — a PAT/App token, NEVER the workflow
#      GITHUB_TOKEN (a GITHUB_TOKEN push succeeds but can never trigger
#      the train; static lint pins every call site's export).
#      RELEASE_TARGET_SHA overrides the tag target (defaults GITHUB_SHA).
#      RELEASE_TRAIN_VERIFY_TRIES (default 12) ×
#      RELEASE_TRAIN_VERIFY_SLEEP seconds (default 10) bound the
#      verification; the test harness shrinks both.
set -euo pipefail

tag="${1:?usage: release_tag_mint.sh <tag>}"
repo="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY:?GITHUB_REPOSITORY must be set}"

# Fail fast BEFORE the cryptic crash: the push URL below collapses to ''
# when GH_TOKEN is unset, and git's `fatal: bad repository ''` does not
# point at the env gap (run 39766453580, v1.0.626 mobile leg).
if [ -z "${GH_TOKEN:-}" ]; then
  echo "::error::tag $tag is missing but GH_TOKEN is not set — the annotated-tag push would run 'git push \"\"'. Set GH_TOKEN (PAT/App token) on the calling step, or the tag can never be minted here." >&2
  exit 1
fi

# Guard 1 — strip the persisted checkout credentials. actions/checkout
# (persist-credentials defaults true) leaves the job token as an
# `http.<host>/.extraheader` in the LOCAL git config; git sends that
# Authorization header on every request to the host, and it outranks the
# URL-embedded GH_TOKEN credentials — the minted push would authenticate
# as GITHUB_TOKEN and the train would never fire (gh-2026). Unset every
# extraheader key the same way the runner's post-job cleanup does.
while IFS= read -r extraheader_key; do
  [ -n "$extraheader_key" ] || continue
  git config --local --unset-all "$extraheader_key" || true
done < <(git config --local --name-only --get-regexp 'http\..*\.extraheader' 2>/dev/null || true)

target="${RELEASE_TARGET_SHA:-${GITHUB_SHA:?}}"
echo "tag $tag missing — minting annotated tag at $target (token-URL push, fires the tag train)"
git fetch origin "$target" --depth=1 2>/dev/null || git fetch origin main --depth=50
# CI checkout carries no identity; annotate as the actions bot without
# touching global config (empty ident → exit 128, run 35426119831).
git -c user.name="github-actions[bot]" \
    -c user.email="41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com" \
    tag -a "$tag" -m "Release $tag" "$target"
# The push is NOT race-idempotent: tags never fast-forward, and the daily
# flow has up to ~5 parallel minters converging on the same missing tag
# (build-macos-cli's two arch legs plus build-extension and both attach
# legs). The loser's push is rejected ("already exists") — that is a WIN
# (a sibling leg minted the same commit), never a failure. Re-probe the
# ref before failing: present → continue to train verification; still
# absent → the push genuinely failed (credential, perms, incident) and
# the leg must go red with a self-explaining error.
if ! git push "${GH_TOKEN:+https://x-access-token:[REDACTED:Connection-String-Password]@github.com/${repo}.git}" "refs/tags/$tag"; then
  if git ls-remote --exit-code origin "refs/tags/$tag" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "tag $tag was minted concurrently by a sibling leg — continuing to train verification"
  else
    echo "::error::tag $tag push failed and the ref is still missing — the push itself failed (credential, permissions, or a GitHub incident), not a race with a sibling leg. No draft will be created; fix the push and re-run." >&2
    exit 1
  fi
fi

# Guard 2 — the train must actually start. A push that fires no workflow
# run (a GITHUB_TOKEN-classed credential on the wire, a GitHub incident, a
# workflow-file mismatch at the tag commit) silently strands every draft
# attached to the tag: green legs, no publish, the sweeper cleans up a day
# later (v1.0.663 / v1.0.665). The run row for the push event appears
# within seconds; poll briefly and fail loud.
tries="${RELEASE_TRAIN_VERIFY_TRIES:-12}"
sleep_s="${RELEASE_TRAIN_VERIFY_SLEEP:-10}"
runs_seen=0
for _ in $(seq 1 "$tries"); do
  sleep "$sleep_s"
  # A probe failure must NOT read as "no train": gh prefers GH_TOKEN (the
  # RELEASE_PAT) for this call, so a fine-grained PAT without Actions:read,
  # an expired PAT, or a rate limit all land here. Swallowing the error
  # (2>/dev/null || echo 0) burns the whole budget and then blames the push
  # credential — a misleading RCA on a red release leg. Fail fast and
  # surface the probe's own output instead.
  # gh can exit 0 yet write a warning to stderr (deprecation/upgrade
  # notice, config warning); merging stderr into the captured value would
  # corrupt the numeric check below ("integer expression expected") and
  # read as "no train" — rolling back a possibly-live tag over a benign
  # warning. Keep stderr OUT of the success value; surface it only on the
  # failure path.
  probe_err="$(mktemp)"
  probe_out="$(gh run list --repo "$repo" --branch "$tag" --limit 10 \
    --json databaseId --jq 'length' 2>"$probe_err")" || {
    echo "::error::train verification probe failed for $tag (gh run list): $(cat "$probe_err") — a failing probe (RELEASE_PAT without Actions:read, expired PAT, rate limit) is NOT evidence of a suppressed train; fix the probe credential before re-running." >&2
    rm -f "$probe_err"
    exit 1
  }
  rm -f "$probe_err"
  if [ "${probe_out:-0}" -gt 0 ]; then
    runs_seen=1
    break
  fi
done
if [ "$runs_seen" -ne 1 ]; then
  # Roll the untrained tag back before failing: the pushed ref left in
  # place would make the prescribed "fix the credential and re-run" skip
  # the mint (and its train check) entirely — the caller's plain
  # `gh release create --draft` would then attach a draft to a ref whose
  # train never ran, silently re-arming the exact stranded-draft shape
  # this script exists to prevent (v1.0.663 / v1.0.665). Drop the LOCAL
  # tag object too: a reused self-hosted workspace would otherwise die at
  # `git tag -a` on the re-run.
  echo "::warning::rolling back the untrained tag ref so a fixed re-run can re-mint" >&2
  git push "${GH_TOKEN:+https://x-access-token:[REDACTED:Connection-String-Password]@github.com/${repo}.git}" ":refs/tags/$tag" ||
    echo "::warning::rollback of refs/tags/$tag failed — a re-run will skip the mint (tag exists) and can strand the draft; delete refs/tags/$tag manually before re-running" >&2
  git tag -d "$tag" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  echo "::error::tag train did not start for $tag: pushed refs/tags/$tag to ${repo} but no workflow run appeared on the ref within the verification budget — the push likely authenticated as a CI-suppressed token (GitHub never fires workflows for GITHUB_TOKEN pushes; the persisted actions/checkout extraheader must not outrank the GH_TOKEN push credentials), or the tag-trigger filter does not match. No draft was created; fix the push credential and re-run." >&2
  exit 1
fi
echo "✅ tag train for $tag started (workflow run visible on the ref) — the draft publish path is live"

- name: Build and package no-sandbox release
        id: package_nosandbox
        env:
          VERSION: ${{ needs.version.outputs.version }}
          ARCH: ${{ matrix.arch }}
          # gh-1865: SHA-1 pin instead of the name-based
          # MACOS_CERTIFICATE_ID secret — build_macos_nosandbox.sh signs
          # via `codesign --sign "${identity}"` and falls back to ad-hoc
          # ("-") when unset, exactly like the old empty-secret path.
          FA_CODE_SIGN_IDENTITY: ${{ steps.signing.outputs.identity_sha1 }}
          FA_DEVELOPMENT_TEAM: ${{ secrets.MACOS_NOTARIZE_TEAM_ID }}
          PROFILE_UUID: ${{ steps.signing.outputs.profile_uuid }}
          PROFILE_TEAM: ${{ steps.signing.outputs.profile_team }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cd flutter_app
          if [ -z "${FA_DEVELOPMENT_TEAM:-}" ] && [ -n "${PROFILE_TEAM:-}" ]; then
            export FA_DEVELOPMENT_TEAM="$PROFILE_TEAM"
          fi
          if [ -n "${PROFILE_UUID:-}" ]; then

flutter_app/scripts/build_macos_nosandbox.sh
#!/bin/bash
# Build a hardened-runtime, *non-sandboxed* macOS release of Fa.
# This flavor can spawn system interpreters (python3, bash, node, etc.)
# and is intended for GitHub Releases, not the App Store.
#
# Usage:
#   scripts/build_macos_nosandbox.sh
#
# Optional environment variables:
#   FA_CODE_SIGN_IDENTITY / MACOS_IDENTITY - signing identity.
#   FA_DEVELOPMENT_TEAM / MACOS_TEAM_ID     - Apple Team ID.
set -euo pipefail

cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."

# Prefer the new FA_* variables; fall back to the older MACOS_* names.
identity="${FA_CODE_SIGN_IDENTITY:-${MACOS_IDENTITY:--}}"
team="${FA_DEVELOPMENT_TEAM:-${MACOS_TEAM_ID:-}}"

# If no identity was requested, try to use a local Apple Development cert so
# the no-sandbox build still has a stable TeamIdentifier for TCC.
if [[ "$identity" == "-" ]]; then
  development_identity=$(security find-identity -v -p codesigning 2>/dev/null \
    | grep -m1 'Apple Development' \
    | sed -n 's/.*"\(.*\)".*/\1/p' || true)
  if [[ -n "$development_identity" ]]; then
    identity="Apple Development"
  fi
fi

# If we have a real identity but no team, extract the team identifier (OU)
# from the matching certificate's subject. HealthKit/HomeKit entitlements
# require a non-empty team.
if [[ "$identity" != "-" && -z "$team" ]]; then
  cert_label=$(security find-identity -v -p codesigning 2>/dev/null \
    | grep -F "$identity" \
    | head -n1 \
    | sed -n 's/.*"\(.*\)".*/\1/p' || true)
  if [[ -n "$cert_label" ]]; then
    team=$(security find-certificate -c "$cert_label" -p 2>/dev/null \
      | openssl x509 -noout -subject 2>/dev/null \
      | grep -oE 'OU=[A-Z0-9]+' \
      | cut -d= -f2 \
      | head -n1 || true)
  fi
fi

# Distribution/Developer ID certificates require manual signing; local
# Apple Development certificates use automatic signing.
if [[ "$identity" == "-" || "$identity" == "Apple Development" ]]; then
  export FA_CODE_SIGN_STYLE="${FA_CODE_SIGN_STYLE:-Automatic}"
else
  export FA_CODE_SIGN_STYLE="${FA_CODE_SIGN_STYLE:-Manual}"
fi

export FA_CODE_SIGN_IDENTITY="$identity"
export FA_DEVELOPMENT_TEAM="$team"
export FA_PROVISIONING_PROFILE_SPECIFIER="${FA_PROVISIONING_PROFILE_SPECIFIER:-}"

readonly APP="build/macos/Build/Products/Release/Fa.app"
readonly ENTITLEMENTS="macos/Runner/ReleaseNoSandbox.entitlements"

echo "[build_macos_nosandbox] Building Release (identity='${identity}', team='${team:-}')..."
flutter build macos --release

echo "[build_macos_nosandbox] Re-signing with no-sandbox entitlements..."
codesign --force \
  --deep \
  --sign "${identity}" \
  --entitlements "${ENTITLEMENTS}" \
  --options runtime \
  "${APP}"

echo "[build_macos_nosandbox] Entitlements now applied:"
codesign -d --entitlements - "${APP}" | grep -E 'app-sandbox|jit|personal-information|homekit|healthkit' || true

echo "[build_macos_nosandbox] Done: ${APP}"

arguments.newText:
# Guard 1 — strip the persisted checkout credentials. actions/checkout
# (persist-credentials defaults true) leaves the job token as an
# `http.<host>/.extraheader` in the LOCAL git config; git sends that
# Authorization header on every request to the host, and it outranks the
# URL-embedded GH_TOKEN credentials — the minted push would authenticate
# as GITHUB_TOKEN and the train would never fire (gh-2026). Unset every
# extraheader key the same way the runner's post-job cleanup does.
while IFS= read -r extraheader_key; do
  [ -n "$extraheader_key" ] || continue
  git config --local --unset-all "$extraheader_key" || true
done < <(git config --local --name-only --get-regexp 'http\..*\.extraheader' 2>/dev/null || true)

# Guard 1b — actions/checkout ≥ v7 (gh-2039, run 41393469972) no longer
# writes the job token as a repo-local extraheader key at all: it writes
# a `git-credentials-<uuid>.config` file under RUNNER_TEMP and references
# it from repo-local `includeIf.gitdir:<gitdir>.path` entries. The sweep
# above then no-ops: `--get-regexp` LISTS the key (git resolves it
# through the include) but the key only EXISTS in the included file, so
# the repo-local unset fails silently under `|| true`. Remove every
# includeIf entry pointing at a credentials config file and delete the
# file — exactly what the runner's post-job cleanup does ("Removing
# includeIf entries pointing to credentials config files").
stripped_v7=0
while IFS= read -r include_key; do
  [ -n "$include_key" ] || continue
  while IFS= read -r include_val; do
    [ -n "$include_val" ] || continue
    case "$include_val" in
      *git-credentials-*.config)
        git config --local --unset-all "$include_key" '.*git-credentials-[^/]*\.config$' || true
        rm -f "$include_val" 2>/dev/null || true
        stripped_v7=1
        ;;
    esac
  done < <(git config --local --get-all "$include_key" 2>/dev/null || true)
done < <(git config --local --name-only --get-regexp 'includeIf\.gitdir:' 2>/dev/null || true)
if [ "$stripped_v7" -eq 1 ]; then
  echo "stripped checkout v7 persisted credentials (includeIf entries + git-credentials config files)"
fi

# Guard 1c — fail loud if an Authorization header STILL resolves for
# github.com after both strips (a scope this script cannot unset: the
# runner user's global/system gitconfig, or a brand-new checkout
# persistence shape). Pushing anyway would authenticate as the
# GITHUB_TOKEN class and strand the release for the sweeper a day later;
# a red leg naming the residual header is the actionable outcome.
residual_header="$(git config --get http.https://github.com/.extraheader 2>/dev/null || true)"
if [ -n "$residual_header" ]; then
  echo "::error::a persisted Authorization header still resolves for github.com after the strip ($(git config --show-origin --get http.https://github.com/.extraheader 2>/dev/null | sed 's/^[^\t]*\t//' || echo 'unknown origin')) — the minted push would authenticate as the CI-suppressed token and no tag train could fire. Remove it (e.g. git config --global --unset-all http.https://github.com/.extraheader) and re-run." >&2
  exit 1
fi

target="${RELEASE_TARGET_SHA:-${GITHUB_SHA:?}}"

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: The daily-publish cli leg (run 41393469972, v1.0.682) failed in two independent jobs — the CLI archive job's tag mint never fired the tag train, and the x86_64 no-sandbox release build died at codesign with `error: 43AEC254FFF1129FBFD09AEA4230320AEF4BA5B0: no identity found`.

**Root cause** (two independent defects):

- **Failure A — tag train (Build macOS CLI arm64, "Archive and upload CLI bundle")**: `scripts/release_tag_mint.sh` Guard 1 strips only repo-LOCAL `http.<host>/.extraheader` keys. actions/checkout has been pinned to **v7.0.1**, which no longer persists the job token that way: the header lives in a separate `git-credentials-<uuid>.config` file under RUNNER_TEMP, referenced from repo-local `includeIf.gitdir:<gitdir>.path` entries (proven by the same run's post-job cleanup log lines: "Removing HTTP extra header" + "Removing includeIf entries pointing to credentials config files"). `git config --local --unset-all` therefore no-ops silently (`|| true`) — `--get-regexp` LISTS the key because git resolves it through the include, but the key only EXISTS in the included file. The Authorization header still rode the wire, outranking the URL-embedded `x-access-token:RELEASE_PAT` credentials (the established gh-2026 wire-precedence premise), so GitHub classed the push as GITHUB_TOKEN and never created a tag-triggered workflow run. The tag-trigger filter itself is healthy — v1.0.681's train fired from an App-token push the same day. Guard 2 correctly rolled back the untrained ref (v1.0.682 deleted at 05:25:46), so no stranded draft resulted from THIS leg's mint (the sibling `build-extension` leg stayed green because its ls-remote saw the tag existing before the rollback and took the plain `gh release create --draft` path — its draft reclaims via the daily sweeper).
- **Failure B — codesign (Build macOS x86_64, "Build and package no-sandbox release")**: `xcode_backend.dart::_codesignFramework` signs `App.framework/App` with raw `codesign --sign <SHA-1>`, which depends entirely on AMBIENT persistent-keychain state (ci-signing.keychain-db unlocked + in the search list) that nothing on the no-sandbox path re-asserts. Timeline: identity verified healthy by `ci-sign install fa-macos` at 06:07:38 (cert valid to 2026-12-30 — expiry ruled out), the same SHA-1 signed the DMG at 06:27:23, then at 06:34:25 — 7m02s after the last keychain activity — codesign found no identity. Nothing from this repo ran on the host in that window; the arm64 leg's identical build passed 30 minutes earlier because its arm64-only TestFlight PKG step incidentally re-ran `ci-sign install` right before its own no-sandbox build — the point-of-use re-assert the x86_64 leg never got (gh-1798's documented principle: "unlock at point of use — immune to any gap length by construction").

**Impact**: The daily publish leg goes red whenever (A) the cli legs mint a missing tag under checkout v7 — every such mint is now structurally dead — or (B) the persistent keychain's ambient state degrades during the ~5-minute no-sandbox build window; v1.0.682 never published.

**Fix approach**:
- `scripts/release_tag_mint.sh`: Guard 1b removes every `includeIf.gitdir:` entry pointing at a `git-credentials-*.config` file and deletes the file (mirroring the runner's own post-job cleanup); Guard 1c fails LOUD if an Authorization header still resolves for github.com after both strips (a residual header would push as GITHUB_TOKEN and strand the release — a red leg naming the residual origin is actionable).
- `.github/workflows/build-macos.yml` (no-sandbox step): gated `~/bin/ci-sign install fa-macos` immediately before the build (idempotent: unlock + identity validity verify + search-list defensive rewrite) — both archs, no longer incidental.
- `flutter_app/scripts/build_macos_nosandbox.sh`: pre-flight `security find-identity -v -p codesigning` against the pinned identity BEFORE the multi-minute flutter build, failing in ~1s with the exact remediation hint.

**Previous attempt**: none — first filing of gh-2039 (the gh-2026 extraheader strip it extended predates this ticket and is insufficient under checkout v7).

- name: Build and package no-sandbox release
        id: package_nosandbox
        env:
          VERSION: ${{ needs.version.outputs.version }}
          ARCH: ${{ matrix.arch }}
          # gh-2039: the point-of-use re-assert below re-imports the
          # identity if it is genuinely gone from the persistent
          # keychain — same env the provisioning step passes to ci-sign
          # (CI_SIGN_P12_* indirection), so the happy path stays a
          # millisecond re-verify and the degraded path self-heals.
          MACOS_CERTIFICATE_P12_BASE64: ${{ secrets.MACOS_CERTIFICATE_P12_BASE64 }}
          MACOS_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.MACOS_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD }}
          CI_SIGN_P12_B64_ENV: MACOS_CERTIFICATE_P12_BASE64
          CI_SIGN_P12_PASSWORD_ENV: MACOS_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD
          # gh-1865: SHA-1 pin instead of the name-based
          # MACOS_CERTIFICATE_ID secret — build_macos_nosandbox.sh signs
          # via `codesign --sign "${identity}"` and falls back to ad-hoc
          # ("-") when unset, exactly like the old empty-secret path.
          FA_CODE_SIGN_IDENTITY: ${{ steps.signing.outputs.identity_sha1 }}
          FA_DEVELOPMENT_TEAM: ${{ secrets.MACOS_NOTARIZE_TEAM_ID }}
          PROFILE_UUID: ${{ steps.signing.outputs.profile_uuid }}
          PROFILE_TEAM: ${{ steps.signing.outputs.profile_team }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cd flutter_app
          # gh-2039 (run 41393469972): the release signing path depends on
          # AMBIENT persistent-keychain state (ci-signing unlocked + in the
          # search list) that raw codesign cannot assert and the 60s unlock
          # watchdog does not guarantee across a multi-minute build window —
          # the x86_64 leg died with "no identity found" at the flutter
          # build's codesign, 7m after the last DMG codesign, while the
          # arm64 leg survived ONLY because its arm64-only PKG step
          # re-ran ci-sign install right before its own build. Re-assert
          # at point of use (gh-1798 principle: immune to any gap length
          # by construction) — idempotent (unlock + identity validity
          # verify + search-list defensive rewrite), gated on the pinned
          # identity so ad-hoc/local runs never require ~/bin/ci-sign.
          if [ -n "${FA_CODE_SIGN_IDENTITY:-}" ]; then
            ~/bin/ci-sign install fa-macos
          fi
          if [ -z "${FA_DEVELOPMENT_TEAM:-}" ] && [ -n "${PROFILE_TEAM:-}" ]; then
            export FA_DEVELOPMENT_TEAM="$PROFILE_TEAM"
          fi
          if [ -n "${PROFILE_UUID:-}" ]; then
            export FA_PROVISIONING_PROFILE_SPECIFIER="$PROFILE_UUID"
          fi
          FLUTTER_XCODE_ARCHS="$ARCH" ./scripts/build_macos_nosandbox.sh

The Guard 1c fired correctly (abort, no push) but the `show-origin` fallback didn't include the origin: my sed fallback swallowed it. Look at my script line:

```bash
echo "::error::a persisted Authorization header still resolves for github.com after the strip ($(git config --show-origin --get http.https://github.com/.extraheader 2>/dev/null | sed 's/^[^\t]*\t//' || echo 'unknown origin')) — ..."
``

`git config --show-origin --get ...` outputs `file:/root/.gitconfig\tAUTHORIZATION: basic ...`. The sed strips up to the first tab → leaves the value, NOT the origin! I stripped the WRONG side. The origin is the part BEFORE the tab. Fix: `sed 's/\t.*//'` to keep the origin (file:...) — or simpler: capture `origin="$(git config --show-origin --get <key> | sed 's/\t.*//')"`. 

Why did the test get `(AUTHORIZATION: basic ...)` — sed `s/^[^\t]*\t//` removed `file:/root/.gitconfig` and kept the value. Fix the sed direction.

arguments.content:
### Root Cause
The cli leg failed in two independent jobs:
- **Tag-train failure (Build macOS CLI arm64)**: actions/checkout **v7** no longer persists the job token as a repo-local `http.<host>/.extraheader` key — it writes a `git-credentials-<uuid>.config` file under RUNNER_TEMP referenced by repo-local `includeIf.gitdir:` entries. `release_tag_mint.sh` Guard 1 only unset repo-local keys, so the strip silently no-op'd, the Authorization header still outranked the URL-embedded RELEASE_PAT credentials, GitHub classed the push as GITHUB_TOKEN, and no tag train ever fired for v1.0.682 (the filter itself is healthy — v1.0.681's train fired the same day).
- **Codesign failure (Build macOS x86_64)**: `xcode_backend`'s raw `codesign --sign <SHA-1>` depends on ambient persistent-keychain state that nothing re-asserts on the no-sandbox path — "no identity found" 7m02s after the last keychain activity, while the identity itself was verified valid at 06:07 and signed the DMG at 06:27. The arm64 leg passed only because its arm64-only TestFlight PKG step incidentally re-ran `ci-sign install` right before its own build.

### Fix
- `scripts/release_tag_mint.sh`: Guard 1b removes `includeIf.gitdir:` entries pointing at `git-credentials-*.config` files and deletes those files (mirrors the runner's own post-job cleanup); Guard 1c fails loud BEFORE pushing if an Authorization header still resolves for github.com (naming the residual origin).
- `.github/workflows/build-macos.yml` (no-sandbox step): gated `~/bin/ci-sign install fa-macos` at point of use before the build (idempotent re-assert: unlock + identity verify + search-list rewrite; self-heals via the CI_SIGN_P12_* env if the identity is genuinely gone), for BOTH archs.
- `flutter_app/scripts/build_macos_nosandbox.sh`: pre-flight `security find-identity -v -p codesigning` against the pinned identity before the multi-minute flutter build — a miss now fails in ~1s with the exact remediation instead of after a 5-minute build.

### Test Coverage
- `test/release_tag_mint_test.dart`: new v7-credentials test (header must no longer resolve, credentials file deleted, tag still lands) — failed before the fix, passes after; new Guard 1c negative (global-scope residual header → abort before any push/probe); 7/7 mint tests pass.
- `test/ci_macos_nosandbox_point_of_use_sign_test.dart` (new): AC1 point-of-use re-assert ordering, AC2 pre-flight presence/ordering.
- Full suite: see run log — no regressions.

### Notes
- The v1.0.682 draft created by the sibling `build-extension` leg (it saw the tag existing before the rollback and skipped the mint) is reclaimed by the daily sweeper (issue #282); the rolled-back ref makes the next run re-mint correctly.
- Guard 1c intentionally reds a leg when an un-strippable Authorization header exists — that push can never fire the train, and a red leg naming the origin is the actionable outcome.
